articles.title: Brasil x Japão: Ancelotti e Raphinha são expulsos em derrota | Ge
articles.standfirst: Seleção se revoltou com árbitro depois de sofrer o terceiro gol do Japão no fim do jogo
articles.summary: Em jogo marcado por golaços de Vini Jr e revolta com a arbitragem, o Brasil perdeu para o Japão e teve Ancelotti e Raphinha expulsos no fim da partida em Singapura.
articles.body:
A seleção brasileira perdeu a cabeça ao levar o terceiro gol do Japão aos 45min do segundo tempo na derrota por 3 a 2 neste sábado , em amistoso em Singapura. O técnico Carlo Ancelotti chegou a invadir o campo para reclamar de falta no lance e foi expulso. Raphinha, que estava no banco, também recebeu cartão vermelho por reclamação.

A Seleção queria que o árbitro Jansen Foo Chuan Hui marcasse falta de Minamino em João Gomes. O volante brasileiro foi desarmado e o Japão chegou ao gol da vitória.

João Gomes sofre falta em lance que originou gol da vitória do Japão sobre o Brasil — Foto: Jeremy Lee / REUTERS

A revolta foi geral do time brasileiro. Quem estava em campo cercou o árbitro. Muitos dos que estavam do lado de fora invadiram o gramado. Ancelotti foi um deles e recebeu de cara o cartão vermelho. Raphinha, um dos mais exaltados, também foi expulso. O atacante não poderá enfrentar Singapura na terça-feira.

Ancelotti, Japão x Brasil — Foto: Jeremy Lee / REUTERS

Durante o jogo a Seleção já vinha reclamando bastante da arbitragem. O Brasil reclamou de falta no primeiro gol sofrido e também pediu pênalti em Raphinha na primeira etapa.

Jogadores do Brasil cercam o árbitro após derrota para o Japão — Foto: Jeremy Lee / REUTERS

A Seleção sofreu 2 a 0 em 18 minutos de jogos. Reagiu e empatou em dois golaços de Vini Jr. de fora da área. Levou no finzinho o gol da vitória japonesa.

articles.title: Raphinha detona arbitragem em Brasil x Japão: "Inadmissível" | Ge
articles.standfirst: Atacante pede desculpas por expulsão contra o Japão, reclama de lances polêmicos e admite que Seleção precisa melhorar
articles.summary: O atacante Raphinha pediu desculpas pela expulsão na derrota do Brasil para o Japão, mas criticou duramente a arbitragem e citou lances polêmicos no amistoso.
articles.body:
Raphinha não escondeu a insatisfação com a arbitragem após a derrota do Brasil, neste sábado, por 3 a 2 para o Japão. Na saída de campo, o atacante pediu desculpas pela expulsão, mas afirmou que houve erros em lances decisivos da partida e classificou a atuação do árbitro como inadmissível. O jogador também reconheceu que a Seleção precisa evoluir.

Mizuho Blue Challenge - Japan v Brazil — Foto: Jeremy Lee / REUTERS

Quero aproveitar e pedir desculpa pela minha atitude e pela expulsão, mas, às vezes, é difícil de controlar depois de, na minha opinião, tantos erros do árbitro dentro do jogo. Vou acreditar que ele errou em muitos momentos do jogo. Só que, cara, é inadmissível — afirmou Raphinha.

A seleção brasileira perdeu a cabeça ao levar o terceiro gol do Japão aos 45min do segundo tempo no amistoso em Singapura. O técnico Carlo Ancelotti chegou a invadir o campo para reclamar de falta no lance e foi expulso. Raphinha, que estava no banco, também recebeu cartão vermelho por reclamação.

A Seleção queria que o árbitro marcasse falta de Minamino em João Gomes. O volante brasileiro foi desarmado e o Japão chegou ao gol da vitória. A revolta foi geral do time brasileiro. Raphinha, um dos mais exaltados, foi expulso. Ao fim da partida, ele citou os lances em que considerou que o árbitro prejudicou a Seleção.

Na minha opinião, o primeiro gol deles teve uma falta ali, que é onde o menino leva a bola com a mão, na minha opinião, foi quatro, mas dá para entender, baseado na série que temos hoje em dia no futebol. Teve o pênalti no primeiro tempo, que, na minha opinião, foi pênalti, onde eu toco a bola e, depois, tiro o apoio nas costas e acabei caindo na área. Na minha opinião, foi pênalti. E, depois, o terceiro gol deles, falta claríssimo em cima do João, onde ele deixou o lance seguir, mas depois o time do Japão recuperou a bola, ele deixou seguir, deixou ele fazer o gol. E, ainda assim, com a ajuda do VAR, ele conseguiu validar o gol. Então, é muito difícil, muito complicado não falar da arbitragem — disse.

Raphinha ainda avaliou a partida feita pela equipe brasileira. Segundo o jogador, o Brasil atuou bem diante do Japão, mas com os erros citados anteriormente fica difícil falar apenas do trabalho que vem sendo desenvolvido.

Acho que a gente fez um grande jogo, muito melhor no segundo tempo do que no primeiro, mas é difícil quando tu joga contra o área, também fica muito complicado. Não estou aqui para tirar a nossa culpa. Como eu falei, a gente tem muita coisa que melhorar e a gente vai melhorar, mas a gente não pode deixar passar em branco a arbitragem que foi hoje — finalizou.

articles.title: UCLA QB Ty Dieffenbach returns in win vs. Illinois after upper body injury
articles.summary: UCLA has already weathered one major quarterback injury. It can only hope it's not facing another.
articles.body:
UCLA has already weathered one major quarterback injury. Fortunately, it appears to have avoided another in a close Big Ten victory.

Ty Dieffenbach, a bright spot for the No. 4-ranked Bruins since starter Nico Iamaleava's knee injury , exited Friday's 22-14 victor y against Illinois with an apparent injury. Third-string quarterback Madden Iamaleava, Nico's brother, replaced him under center with UCLA up 10-0.

The injury occurred less than a minute before halftime, when Dieffenbach took a hard hit from Illinois defensive lineman Carter Janki on an incomplete pass. Dieffenbach was writhing on the ground while holding his left shoulder, then had to be helped off the field and into the blue tent.

He moved to the locker room at halftime, with a clear limp. There was no sign of him at the start of the third quarter, with Iamaleava continuing to lead the UCLA offense.

The Fox Sports broadcast later reported Dieffenbach had sustained an upper body injury and was questionable to return. He re-entered the game later in the third quarter, with the Bruins up 12-7.

He threw a 26-yard touchdown pass to Semaj Morgan early in the fourth quarter to put UCLA ahead 19-7. Dieffenbach finished 13 for 20 for 232 yards, 2 touchdowns and 1 interception.

Dieffenbach transferred to UCLA from Cal Poly last offseason and sat second on the QB depth chart until the elder Iamaleava went down in Week 6 against Oregon. Since then, the Bruins' offense has barely missed a beat with Dieffenbach reeling off four straight wins in his first four starts before this week.

UCLA (10-0) is in the thick of the College Football Playoff race and is one of two remaining undefeated teams in the FBS, alongside No. 2 Utah.

A three-star recruit out of Agoura Hills, California, Dieffenbach began his college career at Pittsburgh but didn't see any game action in his first two seasons. He started 12 games for Cal Poly last year, posting 1,305 passing yards, a 56.8% completion rate, 9 touchdowns and 9 interceptions.

articles.title: Bebeto, con MARCA: "El Dépor debe preocuparse ahora por no bajar nunca más"
articles.standfirst: Entrevista exclusiva en México con la leyenda brasileña del equipo coruñés
articles.summary: Entrevista exclusiva en México con la leyenda brasileña del equipo coruñés
articles.body: José Roberto Gama de Oliveira, Bebeto, (Salvador de Bahía, 1964) es un símbolo de aquel Dépor que, en su caso, ganó Copa y Supercopa (1995) con 102 goles en 154 partidos de 1992 a 1996. Fue campeón del mundo (1994) en una dupla mágica con Romario. Nos atiende en México con motivo del Salón de la Fama de Pachuca. Pregunta. ¿Cómo está viendo a ‘su’ Deportivo? Respuesta. Estoy muy feliz de que haya vuelto a Primera, de donde nunca debió de haber salido. Fueron momentos muy complicados, cuando en años pasados veía al Dépor en la tercera categoría o en Segunda. No me creía verle en esas divisiones. Yo siempre estuve acostumbrado a ver a mi equipo en la élite y de ahí no debe salir. P. ¿Ve todos sus partidos? R. Siempre que puedo, los partidos del Dépor están en mi agenda los fines de semana. Yo siempre estoy acompañando al que es el equipo de mis amores. La Liga española es, para mí, la más fuerte del mundo. Siempre será la mejor por los recuerdos que me trae. P. ¿Qué siente cuando el Dépor marca un gol y usted lo ve desde Brasil? R. ¡Dios mío! Ese equipo es parte de mi historia futbolística y La Coruña es mi casa también. Tengo un cariño muy grande por toda la ciudad, por el club y por todo el pueblo gallego. El Dépor va a estar siempre dentro de mi corazón. P. Su historia allí es idílica: títulos, Pichichi 1993, aquel ‘sub’ tras el polémico penalti fallado por Djukic... pero algún aficionado le afea haberse ido luego al Sevilla [jugó sólo seis partidos allí]. R. Yo necesitaba estar en Brasil en aquel momento y por eso me tuve que ir de La Coruña. Mi abuela había fallecido y debía estar en Río. Después, intenté regresar al Dépor y tenía arreglado todo con el presidente Lendoiro, pero no acabó firmando, pese a que estaba todo listo y yo estaba como loco por volver. Desafortunadamente no se pudo hacer y me fui a Sevilla. P. ¿Y qué pasó allí? R. Sevilla fue un lío tremendo. José Antonio Camacho, el técnico, habló conmigo, y se portó muy bien. Me dijo que la situación no estaba bien y estuvo ‘de 10’ conmigo. P. Volviendo al Dépor, ¿le gusta Yeremay? R. Tiene mucha calidad y me gusta mucho como juega. Estoy deseando que pueda ayudar al equipo muchos años, pero el Dépor debe tener cuidado pues habrá muchas ofertas por él. P. ¿Cree que alguna vez podrá volver el ‘SúperDepor’ que usted vivió? R. La gente quiere eso, que el club llegue más lejos, como antes. P. Pero la Liga ya es cosa de cuatro o cinco equipos, incluyendo los puestos europeos. Está más difícil llegar a los puestos de arriba. R. La Liga siempre fue fuerte. Barca y Real Madrid dominaron siempre, pero en estos momentos, lo más importante es que el Deportivo se mantenga y no baje a Segunda. Primero, hay que pensar en eso. Tener una estabilidad en Primera y a partir de ahí, nunca más salir de la gran élite. Mi preocupación es que no baje nunca más y así irá generando más confianza año tras año. P. ¿Cómo recuerda sus enfrentamientos contra el Real Madrid y el Barcelona? R. Me gustaba mucho jugar contra los grandes. En esos partidos sentía que mis compañeros estaban muy preocupados por jugar ante esos equipazos, pero cuando yo llegué, les convencí de que podíamos ganarles. Y así ocurrió, por ejemplo, en aquel 3-2 histórico contra el Real Madrid en el que empezamos perdiendo con un 0-2. Y poco después, vino el Barça y le ganamos 1-0, y yo hice el gol también. A partir de ahí, creo que el equipo cambió su mentalidad y con mis compañeros sentíamos que les podíamos ganar a todos. P. MARCA sacó una portada icónica con su mano extendida tras los cinco goles que le marcó al Albacete en 1995. ¿Qué recuerda de aquello? R. Entonces fue un récord en la Liga. En los últimos minutos [del 83 al 89] hice cuatro goles, casi uno en cada minuto. Es imposible que me olvide de aquel día. Fue un momento muy especial en mi carrera y tengo guardada esa portada de MARCA con la mano extendida con los cinco goles. Histórico. P. Usted tuvo una relación muy especial con John Benjamin Toshack, uno de sus entrenadores en La Coruña. ¿Es verdad que le prometió quedarse más días en Brasil por cada gol que metiese? R. Sí. Y aquel día que lo prometió marqué tres goles [risas]... y el ‘míster’ cumplió con su palabra y me dejó unos días más en Brasil. El único problema que tuve en mis últimos meses en el Dépor es que necesitaba estar mucho en Brasil por el tema de mi abuela. Y por eso, Toshack me prometió más días por cada gol. Fue una etapa muy bonita de mi vida. P. Acaba de entrar en el Salón de la Fama de México. ¿Lo valora? R. Mucho. Gracias a todo el Grupo Pachuca por esta distinción que, gracias a Dios, me hace recordar que fui feliz.

images.caption: Bebeto, con algunas portadas de MARCA de su época. JUAN CASTRO

articles.title: SEC postpones Ole Miss-Oklahoma game to Sunday following FAA ground stop, Sooners AD responds with blistering statement
articles.summary: Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny claimed the SEC threatened the Sooners with a forfeit if they didn't agree to play Sunday.
articles.body:
One of the larger effects of the FAA's hours-long ground stop Friday was the havoc it wrought on the weekend's sports schedule , particularly in college football.

Many games will be played later than planned Saturday to accommodate the road team's delayed travel schedule . An SEC clash between No. 14 Ole Miss and Oklahoma, however, got pushed all the way back to Sunday.

Previously scheduled for 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday, the Rebels-Sooners clash will now kick off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday, in the thick of the NFL slate. In its statement announcing the decision, the SEC said Ole Miss was unable to depart Oxford on Friday night and the team now can't leave until Saturday afternoon.

The Oklahoma athletic department was, to put it mildly, not happy.

Immediately after the SEC announced the postponement, athletic director Roger Denny released a lengthy statement complaining about Ole Miss' inability to travel Friday, "unlike every other team traveling for competition tomorrow," and noting the effect the delay would have on fans.

Denny also revealed that SEC commissioner Greg Sankey threatened Oklahoma with a forfeit if it didn't go along with the new schedule. The full statement can be read below.

No. 14 Ole Miss enters the game clinging to College Football Playoff hopes, while unranked Oklahoma is all but eliminated at 5-4.

Oklahoma athletic director Roger Denny's statement on Ole Miss postponement

We recognize the extraordinary circumstances surrounding the ground stoppage and understand the challenges it created for teams across the country. As soon as we learned of Ole Miss' travel issues, we immediately began communicating with their staff and our conference leadership. We were told that Ole Miss explored every avenue to travel to Norman and play on Saturday as planned. But, unlike every other team traveling for competition tomorrow, they were unable to find a solution. After multiple conversations with the league office, Commissioner Sankey informed us of his decision to move our game to Sunday, over our strong objection. After continued discussions, he further informed us that our failure to play on Sunday at the directed time would result in a forfeit. Rescheduling the game has a significant impact, particularly on our fans. Those who have made travel arrangements, accommodations, and personal plans around a Saturday game now face unnecessary disruption and hardship. Their time, commitment, and investment deserve greater consideration than they were afforded in the conference's decision tonight. I understand that difficult decisions sometimes must be made under extraordinary circumstances. But those decisions must also consider the impact on everyone involved. Put simply, this decision isn't fair to our athletes, our institution, or to Sooner Nation. But we've been given no other choice. We are obligated to play the game when directed, but we remain steadfast in our belief that the wrong outcome was reached this evening. We will continue to fight in the best interests of OU Athletics and always on behalf of our student-athletes and fans. On Saturday, we will share more on game logistics and fan appreciation measures. articles.title: Melvine Malard & Sonia Bompastor: How Chelsea reunion has brought best in France striker
articles.summary: Chelsea striker Melvine Malard and manager Sonia Bompastor tell the story of their 12-year footballing relationship.
articles.body:
Thousands of miles from home, a 14-year-old had an encounter that would change her life.

Nestled in a forest about an hour from Paris is France's national football academy at Clairefontaine. Famous for developing global stars such as Kylian Mbappe and Thierry Henry, it is also where a teenage Melvine Malard first met Sonia Bompastor in 2014.

Malard had travelled from Reunion Island, a French overseas territory in the Indian Ocean, to play in a football tournament. Watching from the sidelines was a titan of French football.

Bompastor, a two-time Champions League winner who had become Lyon's head of youth development, spotted the young forward and persuaded her to move to mainland France.

Twelve years later, the pair have been reunited at Chelsea. After joining from Manchester United in July, Malard has already established herself as a key player.

It took just six appearances for the 26-year-old to match her six-goal tally from last season's Women's Super League, helping fill the void left by Sam Kerr's departure.

"I knew she had the potential to be a really good player," Bompastor tells BBC Sport. "Having known her for so long and all the hard work she has put in, I'm really proud of her."

'It's so cold here!' - Malard's initial thoughts on Europe

Convincing Malard's mother to let her daughter move nearly 6,000 miles from home was not straightforward - but Bompastor had a plan for the phone call.

"It's a lot of responsibility for you as a coach to bring a young player like this and move her from her own family," Bompastor says.

"The main thing for her mum in that phone call was she knew she could trust me as a manager but also as a woman."

For teenager Malard, the transition was difficult. She was close to her family and struggled with the bitterly cold winters of Lyon.

Because of its tropical climate, temperatures on Reunion Island rarely drop below 20C even in winter, whereas in Lyon, the mercury remains in low single figures during December and January.

Bompastor still laughs about one particular conversation with the young forward.

"She said to me: 'I'm so sorry, Sonia, but I think I need to go back to my place. It's so cold here. I can't play football any more!'" says Bompastor.

But Malard stuck around, knowing the opportunity was too good to turn down.

"When Lyon calls you, it's maybe just one time in your life," she says. "So you need to take your opportunity when it comes."

Bompastor's influence extended beyond football. As head of Lyon's academy, she also kept a close eye on Malard's education.

"When I did bad in school, she called me," Malard says. "'Mel, where are you? The school called me - it's not good what you're doing!'

"That was a nightmare - Sonia is always here."

Their relationship continued as Malard progressed through the ranks and finally broke into Lyon's first team as a 17-year-old in 2017.

By the time Bompastor had become the club's head coach for the 2021-22 season, Malard had established herself in the team and at the end of that campaign, she started the Champions League final against Barcelona as Bompastor's side secured a 3-1 victory.

For the boss, it remains a particularly special memory.

"When you look at all the journey and Melvine coming as a young kid into a different environment, far away from her family... and how she improved to be starting that game and for us to win that game," Bompastor says. "It's a big achievement."

Title race hots up before Chelsea-Man City showdown

Cast your vote for BBC Women's Footballer of the Year 2026

Now reunited with her former boss at Chelsea, Malard has relished the responsibility of leading the line following Kerr's departure.

It took her just 341 minutes to chalk up six league goals for her new club. Last season, despite scoring four in the first two games, it was 17 matches and 1,206 minutes before she hit the same number for Manchester United.

Goals have come alongside frequently getting into dangerous positions.

At United in 2025-26, she averaged 3.4 shots and 6.2 touches in the opposition penalty area per 90 minutes. Those figures have risen to 5.4 and 11.8 respectively at Chelsea.

The quality of her opportunities has also improved. Her expected goals per 90 minutes have more than doubled from 0.5 to 1.1, while her shot conversion rate has increased from 10.5% to 22.2%.

It suggests Malard is benefiting from more opportunities in dangerous areas, while also making better use of the chances that come her way.

Bompastor believes the forward's improvement has been about more than just her goalscoring ability.

"She developed herself in terms of technical skills, knowledge of the game, understanding the game a little bit more, reading the game better," she says.

"She can play in different positions so we know we can use her as a nine or as a winger."

Such versatility has made Malard a valuable option for Bompastor as she chases silverware at home and abroad.

After winning the domestic treble during her first season in 2024-25, Chelsea only picked up the League Cup last season, with their third-placed finish snapping a run of six straight WSL titles.

Nine games into 2026-27, the Blues have the league's best attack and meanest defence, but a disappointing draw at home to Everton last weekend allowed champions Manchester City to overhaul them at the top of the table.

The two sides meet at Stamford Bridge on Saturday in a match live on BBC One that could be instrumental in deciding the title.

Malard will likely be leading the line, but Bompastor's ambitions for her former academy prospect are not limited to club level.

When Malard asks what Bompastor hopes she will achieve this season, the Chelsea boss sets her a clear challenge.

"I would like you to play for France next summer as the number nine and to win the World Cup," she says.

Twelve years after their first encounter, Bompastor continues to push Malard to new heights.

articles.title: Will John McGinn take Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law's joint record for most Scotland goals?
articles.summary: After drawing level with Hughie Gallacher on 24 Scotland goals, will midfielder John McGinn reach Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law's record tally of 30?
articles.body:
As Scotland legend Kenny Dalglish watched one of his records equalled in Scotland's 2-1 win over North Macedonia, another of his feats loomed into view.

The night was supposed to be about Andy Robertson joining Dalglish as Scotland's most-capped man, the Tottenham left-back making his 102nd appearance for his country.

But instead, for the first time, the 75-year-old might be nervous that his crown as one of Scotland men's all-time top goalscorers is wobbling.

That is because, in Scotland's rather humdrum Nations League victory, John McGinn - in his 94th Scotland appearance - took two big strides towards the record.

The Aston Villa midfielder now has 24 goals for his country - six shy of Dalglish's long-standing record of 30, shared with Denis Law.

"It's something that's been in the back of my head," McGinn admitted in the post-match debrief. "If I start climbing that table, it means we've been successful as a team."

Now 32 years old, time is running out for him. But as he pulls level with Hughie Gallacher, one of the Wembley Wizards of folklore, his ambition is clear.

McGinn double gives drab Scotland win over North Macedonia

McGinn 'definitely capable' of reaching record

There was a time when talk of this record being toppled seemed laughable. Scotland has produced strikers in recent decades, but none close to Dalglish or Law.

The fact a midfielder might take the title makes McGinn's feat all the more astonishing.

His prowess in front of goal is no secret to the Tartan Army. There was the spell at the end of 2019 where he scored six in three games, his overhead kick against Austria, his late winner against Croatia in 2024.

But of late, his lack of goals and even his performances have had some fans questioning where he fits into the Scotland team.

"It has been a bit of a dry patch for me over the last year on the goal front," McGinn admitted, and he's not wrong.

He failed to find the back of the net for Scotland in 2025, the first time he'd done that since 2020.

But, just as his form at Villa has sky-rocketed, he came up big for his new international head coach Sebastien Pocognoli.

"Isn't it great to have a John McGinn in your team?" former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on Sportsound. "He's somebody you'd want to have in your team to be taking a penalty for you.

"I'd be surprised if John McGinn doesn't get the goal record now. It might take him another year or two, but he is definitely capable of getting that record."

Becoming Scotland's main penalty taker will help, a fact McGinn alluded to coyly post-match.

In his career, he had only taken one spot-kick before this season - scoring for Scotland in the 3-3 draw against Norway back in 2023.

In this campaign he has scored three and missed one, smacking the bar against Fulham on Halloween.

In classic McGinn fashion, he bounced back to slot home against Manchester United the following week, before being caught on ref-cam admitting to the official that he was nervous to take it after his hitting the woodwork.

That jovial, lovable personality has not just won him fans off the pitch. It is clear that his team-mates at both Villa and the national team adore him.

"He's not going to stop until he [gets the record]," said striker Che Adams, who helped set up McGinn's first against North Macedonia.

"Everyone's pleased for him, he's the best person I've met in football. For him to get the recognition he deserves is amazing."

McGinn's iconic status in Scottish football is secure and will not be tarnished if he fails to climb the mountain.

Whether it is being speared by Steven Thompson in training, calling Scotland performances 'jobby', or admitting he would "probably be at Yeovil" were it not for his backside, the midfielder has already won the heart of a nation.

articles.title: Mikautadze confiesa su amor por el Barça: "Es el club de mi corazón"
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Villarreal desea poder vestir algún día la camiseta azulgrana
articles.summary: El delantero del Villarreal desea poder vestir algún día la camiseta azulgrana
articles.body: El nombre de Georges Mikautadze sonó con fuerza en el tramo final del mercado de fichajes de cara a una posible llegada al Barça, que seguía sin poder traer a Julián Alvarez. El georgiano no acabó en la Ciudad Condal, pero eso no afectó al tremendo amor que sigue por el club azulgrana. Así lo manifestó el delantero en una entrevista para DAZN. Mikautadze, que poco a poco se va haciendo un nombre cada vez más grande en el Villarreal, fue preguntado por aquel interés que hubo del Barça en verano y el futbolista no dudó en mostrar su gran afecto a equipo que dirige Hansi Flick. “Es halagador. El Barça, es el club de mi corazón, los miro jugar desde que era pequeño. Todavía veo sus partidos ahora”, comentó el atacante de 26 años, que lleva cinco goles en lo que llevamos de temporada sumando los tres de Liga y dos más en Champions. Mikautadze sigue soñando con poder vestir la camiseta azulgrana y para eso trabaja: “A mí me toca seguir trabajando para tener, por qué no, la oportunidad de unirme a un gran club como ese. Pienso que tengo cualidades para convertirme en uno de los mejores delanteros de LaLiga”.

articles.title: Scottish gossip: Steve Clarke and Christian Titz on Aberdeen manager shortlist
articles.summary: Steve Clarke and Christian Titz are reportedly on Aberdeen's shortlist to replace Stephen Robinson as manager.

articles.title: Nigel Clough: Is Mansfield Town manager's longevity a landmark achievement or an indictment on football?
articles.summary: Mansfield boss Nigel Clough discusses his longevity and staying power as he becomes a club's longest-serving manager for a second time in his career.
articles.body:
Becoming the longest-serving manager at a club takes some doing in the fickle world of football.

Sticking around at two clubs long enough to hold that mantle is just about unprecedented.

But Mansfield Town's Nigel Clough is about to redefine longevity as a manager when it comes to working at sides that make up the top 92 in the English pyramid.

"I don't think it's particularly an achievement; I think it's more an indictment of football that nobody else has lasted that long," Clough told BBC Sport.

This weekend he becomes the longest-serving manager – in terms of active years in the job and league matches at the helm – of the Stags, where he surpasses club great Ian Greaves.

The 16 years Clough spent at Burton Albion, which took in around 900 matches across two spells spanning more than two decades, means the record at the east Staffordshire side is already his.

Former England forward Clough is now six years and one week into the Stags job and is the second longest-serving manager across England's top four leagues - behind only Mikel Arteta at Arsenal - but he does not see his staying power as anything special.

"I don't really think about it that much, I have to say. I'm just trying to get through the week," said Clough, who has been in charge of Mansfield for 329 matches across all competitions.

While Clough's players, as well as Mansfield fans have a different take on what his lengthy tenure at the One Call Stadium has meant, the 60-year-old reeled off the names of legendary past managers - his late father and iconic Nottingham Forest boss Brian Clough included - when reflecting on what joy clubs would have by sticking by their manager.

"When you look back 20 or 30 years, my dad was at Forest for 18 years, Alex Ferguson was at Manchester United for so long and then there was Arsene Wenger at Arsenal. That was at the top level, but even lower down there was a lot of managers who stayed a lot of years," he said

"I just think it's sad the way football is going at the moment. The first bad period that people have, a month, two months or something like that, and the manager is the one that goes."

Clough, who played in the top flight for Forest, Liverpool and Manchester City, has been in management for 28 years and been in charge of just four clubs - Mansfield, Burton, Derby County and Sheffield United - in that time.

Since bounding from non-league level - where he spent the first 10 years of his management career in his first spell at Burton - to take the reins of Derby in the Championship in 2009, no-one has overseen more matches than Clough's 893 across England's top four divisions.

The latest statistics from the League Managers' Association show that managers across those leagues are now staying in their jobs for less than a year on average.

Clough bucking the trend with his record-setting endurance at Mansfield comes in the same week that Manchester United sacked Michael Carrick, when he was 10 months into the job, and Crystal Palace relieved Pierre Sage of his role after only 16 games.

When asked if Clough has ever felt his job was under threat during any "sticky period" at Mansfield, he responded with a firm "of course".

It was when the Stags were in the relegation places and on a 12-match winless run in his first full campaign in charge in 2021-22.

He survived that, then oversaw a club-record 11 consecutive home wins and went on to guide Mansfield to the League Two play-off final at Wembley later the same season.

"You've got to go through that period and you've got to get through it," Clough said of dealing with difficult runs as a manager.

"And I think as you get a little bit older, you know more that it's going to change.

"You get a result out of adversity as much as anything. If you're winning, it doesn't keep going, and if you're losing it's the same thing if you've got a reasonable team and you're doing the right things."

Clough: 'Six years have gone extremely quickly'

Mansfield boss Clough on 25 years 'in family business'

What do fans and players think of Clough?

While Mansfield missed out on promotion when they took their bid all the way to the national stadium in 2022, they went up automatically two years later when they finished third in the table.

It ended Mansfield's 21-year absence from the third tier. And when he kept them up in their first season back, Clough did what no-one had done for 35 years.

Last season they finished 10th, the club's highest league placing since 1987 when Greaves guided them to exactly the same position in the standings.

Stags supporter Dean Foulkes says it "has been an incredible journey" at Mansfield since Clough took the helm in November 2020.

At Burton he is a club legend for the way he transformed the Brewers as a non-league side in his first spell there before taking them to the Championship during his second stint.

He leapt a number of divisions when he left Burton the first time to manage Derby - a particularly poignant job as his father took the Rams to their first English title in 1972.

Even at Sheffield United, where Clough had the shortest stint of his managerial career, he guided them to the semi-final of the FA Cup when they were a League One side in 2014.

"He is really good football man to have around. We should be proud that he is Mansfield Town manager," Foulkes told BBC Radio Nottingham.

"Look at what he has achieved, promotion, and we now have players coming to Mansfield Town because they want to play for Nigel Clough."

It is why prolific veteran forward David McGoldrick moved there in the summer, and how the club has enticed former Leeds United forward Tyler Roberts, as well as ex-Preston forward Michael Smith to the Nottinghamshire town while also landing highly-rated Tottenham midfielder George Abbott on loan.

Ryan Sweeney says the chance to play for Clough was "the main reason" he decided to return to the club last summer.

Former Nottingham Forest and Southend striker Stephen McLaughlin says Clough "manages differently to any other manager" he has worked with.

"He doesn't treat you as a number, he treats you as a person and you want to run though bricks walls for him," McLaughlin said.

"It's hard to explain what he does for you on and off the pitch as well. You are not on the grass too long in training because he trusts you to get your work in and to be ready for Saturday.

"He doesn't give too much tactical information to people because the message is 'just do your job and work hard'."

Jordan Bowery has been asked to do that more than most, having been transformed from a striker to a defender and is now seen as 'Mr Versatile'. , external

"He is incredibly loyal and trusts me in those positions," Bowery said. "A lot of managers wouldn't do that, but he's had my back and I appreciate that.

"He can get onto you, but that is like most managers. He expects and demands the best out of every single one of you each day.

"He has obviously been around the game a long time, played at the highest level - he knows the game and he knows the players."

'Insight into success' a family business

And Clough, the player, is a former attacker of considerable repute in Nottinghamshire.

No-one has scored more than Clough's 131 goals for Forest over the past 113 years.

It was there, at Mansfield's high-profile county neighbours, where he thrived under his father who famously guided the Reds to the First Division title in 1978 before collecting back-to-back European Cups.

The manager that Clough is has been shaped by the successes he watched up close as a child and those he later revelled in as a player.

"When you're brought up in the household that we were brought up in and the environment we were brought up in, then we have a certain insight into what it takes to have a chance of being successful and what you expect of the team and everything," he said.

"And the empathy, I don't think you should ever forget that if you've been a player as well, how that feels when you have a rough time and so on."

And it is those players, and how they are found before investing in them that is the closest thing to revealing the secret to Clough's longevity.

"We don't like wasting the owners' money," he said.

"Whether it was at Burton when we were in the Dr Martens South [non-league level] or whether it's here at Mansfield Town, we try and look after it as best we can. And we have a responsibility to do that.

"We do as much in-depth research as we can on players. Character is the main feature of what we look at. We can see all the stuff on the videos of what they can do, then we watch them live and everything, but you have to delve really into the character and get a lot of references from players, coaches, managers.

"We take that very seriously. Each season we set out to just try and get a few better players in the squad.

"It's keeping the ball rolling, keeping the owners happy, keeping the supporters happy."

Additional reporting by BBC Radio Nottingham's David Jackson and Jake Garner.

articles.title: El último desafío del 'hombre del año': derrotar a la campeona del mundo
articles.standfirst: Harry Kane posa con sus recientes portadas de MARCA antes de visitar a La Roja en Madrid
articles.summary: Harry Kane posa con sus recientes portadas de MARCA antes de visitar a La Roja en Madrid
articles.body: Harry Kane es el ‘hombre del año’... si excluimos a los jugadores campeones del mundo con España, porque, por algo, La Roja es la número uno, y en MARCA debemos darle valor a esa segunda estrella de nuestro país. Pero, sin españoles, no hay jugador en el mundo que le haga sombra a Harry Kane (HK) durante este año 2026 en el ‘planeta fútbol’. Y así lo ha reflejado nuestro diario con cuatro portadas dedicadas, en mayor o menor medida, al delantero del Bayern Múnich. Las portadas empezaron este pasado verano con la Bota de Oro 2025-26 por sus 36 goles en la pasada Bundesliga; continuaron con una entrevista exclusiva concedida a MARCA en Múnich en la que Kane indicaba lo siguiente: “No me gusta hablar de mí, pero mis goles hablan por sí solos”; la tercera portada vino con el Premio ‘Los 100 de MARCA’, ganado por HK tras la votación de un panel de expertos consultados por este periódico; y el culmen llegó con el histórico Balón de Oro que recogió Harry en Londres hace poco más de dos semanas y media. El exdelantero del Tottenham llega de nuevo a Madrid para jugar como capitán de Inglaterra ante La Roja de Luis de la Fuente. Lo hace como principal amenaza deportiva de los ingleses ante una Selección que lleva 43 partidos consecutivos sin perder y que ya demostró su poderío en el pasado Mundial, en el que los ‘Three Lions’ terminaron en tercer lugar, sólo por detrás de España y la Argentina de Messi. Kane arriba al estadio Metropolitano apenas 10 días después de pasar por encima del Atlético de Madrid con un Bayern que fue muy superior en ese partido de Champions ganado por los alemanes (0-2). Es cierto que HK no marcó aquel día ante Jan Oblak, pero sí dio la asistencia del 0-2 a Laimer, y cuajó un buen partido para los de Vincent Kompany bajando mucho al mediocampo y construyendo gran parte del juego en tres cuartos del equipo muniqués. Fue una muestra de lo que puede dar de sí Harry en el Metropolitano en el choque de mañana. Kane llega con el áurea no sólo de ser el ‘jugador del año’ para el mundo del fútbol (volviendo a exceptuar a los cracks de La Roja), sino con el reciente reconocimiento de ser el futbolista inglés con más internacionalidades en la historia de su país (126), cosa que ratificará en el Metropolitano en un récord que ya presume de forma individual como el más internacional de los ‘Three Lions’. El homenaje que le rindió Wembley el pasado jueves no es más que el reconocimiento al que Gary Lineker, otra leyenda inglesa, ya ha denominado como el “mejor jugador inglés de la historia de nuestro país”. Así lo dijo. Kane llega a Madrid con un bagaje goleador impresionante en los últimos años, que no hubiera sido posible sin la ayuda profesional, desde hace siete años, de su doctor deportivo personal, el madrileño Alejandro Elorriaga, con el que ha superado hace meses sus históricos problemas de tobillo y al que dedicó buena parte de su discurso de agradecimiento del Balón de Oro con estas palabras: “Le agradezco mucho el trabajo que hemos hecho fuera de los focos y el tiempo que me ha dedicado para que yo pueda rendir de esta forma últimamente”. Y es que el rendimiento goleador de HK ha ido incrementándose con los años. Basta saber estos datos: en las últimas cuatro temporadas, desde que está en el Bayern, sus goles totales han sido: 44 en la 23-24; 41 en la 24-25; 61 en la pasada campaña; y los 10 que lleva en ésta, sólo contando las dianas a nivel de clubes. Con estos números llega mañana a Madrid un tal Harry Kane, el 'hombre del año'.

articles.title: Portugal plan special Ronaldo tribute: Entire squad to wear No. 7 shirts, Denmark game to pause in seventh minute
articles.summary: Portugal plans to honor Cristiano Ronaldo with a unique tribute during his farewell match against Denmark, featuring the entire squad in No. 7 shirts and a moment of applause in the seventh minute.
articles.body: Portugal are preparing a series of tributes to Cristiano Ronaldo when they face Denmark in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday, marking the end of an international career that lasted more than two decades. The Portuguese Football Federation has approved a collective gesture involving every player in the squad, while supporters at the Estadio Municipal de Braga will also have an opportunity to honour their former captain during the match.Portugal players to wear Cristiano Ronaldo's No. 7 shirt against DenmarkThe most visible part of the tribute will come before kick-off, when every member of Portugal's squad is expected to wear the No. 7 shirt associated with Ronaldo as the team walks out at the Estadio Municipal de Braga.The decision was reportedly finalised during a meeting on Thursday involving Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proença, national team head coach Jorge Jesus and the senior leadership group. The players involved in the discussions included captains Bernardo Silva, Rúben Dias and Bruno Fernandes.According to Portuguese newspaper A Bola, the meeting brought together the federation's leadership and coaching staff to determine how best to recognise Ronaldo's contribution following his announcement of international retirement on November 5.The tribute will extend beyond the pre-match walk-out. The match is also scheduled to be paused in the seventh minute, allowing supporters to rise and applaud the former captain. UEFA has reportedly granted special permission for the gesture, giving fans at the Braga stadium an opportunity to recognise the player whose number has become synonymous with Portuguese football.Ronaldo's attendance remains unconfirmed, so it is not yet clear whether he will be present to witness the ceremony himself.Jorge Jesus explains who organised Portugal's farewell to RonaldoJesus addressed the arrangements during his pre-match press conference, making clear that the tribute was a decision taken by the federation rather than one organised independently by the coaching staff.“Such decisions are always the responsibility of the Portuguese Football Federation, more specifically its football and sporting departments and its president,” Jesus said.The Portugal coach also spoke about the scale of Ronaldo's contribution, pointing to the 23 years he spent representing the national team and the influence he had beyond the country.“It is brilliant because nobody can forget the 23 years Cris spent with the national team, what he achieved for Portugal, and the impact he has had on the world of football,” Jesus added.The federation has also decided to leave vacant the room Ronaldo used at Cidade do Futebol, Portugal's national team training complex. The gesture is intended to preserve a symbolic place for the former captain within the squad during the first international break following his retirement.The arrangements come as Portugal begin preparing for a future without the player who has been central to their national team for much of the modern era. Bruno Fernandes and Bernardo Silva are among the experienced figures expected to assume greater leadership responsibilities, although Ronaldo's departure leaves a significant gap in both the squad's history and its attacking record.Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal records after 23 years and 146 goalsRonaldo retired from international football with 146 goals in 234 appearances, records that leave him as the leading goalscorer and most-capped player in the history of men's international football.His Portugal debut came on August 20, 2003, against Kazakhstan, beginning a career that concluded on September 24, 2026. Across those 23 years, he became the defining figure of a generation that delivered the country's first European Championship title and two Nations League triumphs.Portugal's victory at Euro 2016 in France was the defining achievement of Ronaldo's international career, followed by Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025. His individual records extended across both major international competitions: he scored 11 goals in 27 World Cup appearances, making him Portugal's leading scorer at the tournament, and established the men's record of 14 goals in European Championship final tournaments.He also became the only player to score at six different men's World Cups, finding the net in Germany in 2006, South Africa in 2010, Brazil in 2014, Russia in 2018, Qatar in 2022 and the 2026 tournament. His combined total of 25 goals across the European Championship and World Cup is another men's international record.Ronaldo scored against 49 different national teams, with Luxembourg conceding 11 goals and Hungary nine. His international record also includes 10 hat-tricks, two of which contained four goals, and 22 converted penalties. Of his 146 goals, 124 came in competitive internationals, excluding friendly matches.Those numbers provide the statistical measure of a career that also included unsuccessful campaigns and difficult tournament exits before Portugal's major successes. The tribute against Denmark will give the federation, the players and supporters an opportunity to recognise the full contribution of a footballer whose influence extended well beyond the records he accumulated.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Thomas Tuchel: England boss to remind players of anti-racism protocols before Spain game
articles.summary: Manager Thomas Tuchel will remind England's players of Uefa's anti-racism protocols before Sunday's Nations League fixture against Spain in Madrid.
articles.body:
Manager Thomas Tuchel will remind England's players of Uefa's anti-racism protocols before Sunday's Nations League fixture against Spain in Madrid.

The match will be England's first in the Spanish capital since a notorious fixture at Real Madrid's Bernabeu stadium in 2004 which was overshadowed by racist chanting aimed at England players.

The Spanish federation was fined last month and ordered to play their next friendly match with a partial stadium closure after fans sang "Islamophobic and xenophobic" chants about Muslims during a game against Egypt.

"We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]," Tuchel said. "There is a protocol in place.

"Maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid]."

European governing body Uefa, the organiser of the Nations League, has a three-step protocol to handle incidents of discrimination inside stadiums, designed to give referees the power to halt matches, and even abandon games if racist behaviour continues.

In the first instance, referees halt the match and request an announcement on the public address system.

Then, if discrimination continues, officials can stop the game for five to 10 minutes and take the players from the field.

If issues continue after the second stoppage, then the game can be abandoned.

"It's important that the players know about the protocol," Tuchel said.

"And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch."

Who would make your England-Spain combined XI?

Sunday's fixture takes place at Atletico Madrid's home, the Metropolitano.

Victory would ensure England win their Nations League group and earn a more favourable quarter-final draw but world champions Spain are unbeaten in 43 matches, including a 3-2 win at Wembley in September.

"It's important that we play with the same mindset that we played at home, and attack them and try to make it a physical game, and try to impose our strength," Tuchel added.

"It [Spain] is a team that has forgotten how to lose, so it requires a top performance first of all, and if we can deliver this performance, it will give us a big boost.

"I think we're there, and I think we're ready to win on Sunday,"

articles.title: Nations League: Northern Ireland targeting 'very difficult challenge' of League A promotion
articles.summary: A win against Ukraine on Saturday night would leave Northern Ireland needing only a point away to Hungary next week to secure promotion to Nations League A for the first time.
articles.body:
Before this Nations League campaign, Northern Ireland had won just one of 16 games played in the second tier of the competition.

But after eight points from four games across September and October, all without conceding a goal, Michael O'Neill's side could end Saturday night as a League A side for the first time.

For that to come to pass, Hungary would need to lose to Georgia in Tbilisi [17:00 GMT] before a Northern Ireland win at home to Ukraine in the later kick-off.

Even if only they hold up their end of the bargain with a win at Windsor Park, the side would travel to Budapest on Tuesday night knowing a point would be good enough to top the group and seal promotion.

"You do look at the teams that do step up and it's tough. We've seen teams do that before and they find it very difficult," said O'Neill after stressing his side would be looking no further than the first game of this double-header.

"But for us to get that opportunity to play against those big teams in a competitive group stage would be great, it would be great for the development of the team.

"I wouldn't say the results at that point wouldn't be important, but I think we'd learn a lot."

Watch on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two NI from19:15 GMT; Listen on BBC Sounds and BBC Radio Ulster; Watch, listen, live text and clips on BBC Sport app & website

Strong performance in the Nations League carries multiple rewards.

Finishing in the top two of their group - something Northern Ireland would confirm with a draw against Ukraine - would ensure O'Neill's side are among the second group of seeds when the draw for Euro 2028 qualifying is made in Belfast next month.

There is also the potential backdoor route into the qualification play-offs too, the same method used by Northern Ireland to find themselves just two games from the summer's World Cup despite finishing third in their group.

But for O'Neill promotion would also bring the less tangible benefit of showing his squad what is required to reach the very top.

O'Neill has previously sought out friendlies against the likes of Spain and France, drawing praise from his then Les Bleus counterpart Didier Deschamps for taking a game against the latter on the eve of the World Cup when others had not been so keen.

Midfielder Shea Charles previously spoke of how going up against the likes of Spain's Rodri in such fixtures helped "prepare" him for the Premier League before he got his £30m move to Fulham.

And O'Neill feels further exposure to such challenges, especially in regular competitive fixtures, would be hugely beneficial to others in his largely inexperienced side.

He added: "That's good for any player, but particularly young players, because it lets them see what's required, what's required to be a Spanish international and playing in the Champions League or playing your club football at the highest level in Europe.

"We want our players to aspire to try to get there too."

Who makes your Northern Ireland XI against Ukraine?

Birthdays and broken lamps - at home with the Charles brothers

NI can draw on strong club form in key window

Barnsley midfielder Patrick Kelly scored his first international goal in that game against France, the strike coming on a night he shared the field with the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele and Michael Olise.

The 22-year-old, who joined the Tykes in the summer of 2025 having not made a senior appearance for West Ham, has played all his club football in either League One, League Two, or the Irish Premiership.

"Playing those bigger nations, it would only improve us as a team," he said.

"You want to test yourself against the best. A couple of the lads have experienced it, they would have played Germany in the last [qualifying ]campaign and done well, and I had it that night against France.

"Playing against the best players in the world, you see where you're at and the team as well."

Having missed that game against France through suspension, Blackburn Rovers defender Tom Atcheson's only international start coming into this campaign had been against Guinea, but the 20-year-old senses the team is ready for the step up.

"I think we do belong there and we're showing it," he said. "We want to have those challenges, we want to challenge ourselves against the best because it's exciting times.

"We know what we're capable of. To get into League A with those massive nations would be unbelievable, that's where we all want to get.

"We're looking forward to the next two games and hopefully to make that happen."

articles.title: Jack Moylan: 'Exciting' midfielder flourishing for club and country
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks as Jack Moylan's terrific form for Cardiff City and Republic of Ireland ahead of the Irish's final two Nations League games.
articles.body:
Jack Moylan made his intent clear when speaking to the media in August soon after joining Cardiff City in the summer from Lincoln City.

He outlined how he wanted to impress for the Welsh club and ensure he was a mainstay in Republic of Ireland squads after winning his first two caps in May.

Fast forward three months and the 25-year-old has certainly come good on those promises by stepping up for club and country.

Under fellow Irish man Brian Barry-Murphy at Cardiff he has netted 11 goals in 17 games in all competitions while also providing three assists.

On the international stage, Moylan featured in all four of Republic of Ireland's Nations League games in the extended September/October window, scoring and assisting in a 3-0 win against Israel.

Already a key player for the Bluebirds, Moylan is emerging as an important attacking threat for his country too and will be pivotal in their final two Nations League games against Austria and Kosovo.

It is the latest chapter in the rapid rise of Moylan, who has gone from strength to strength since earning a move to Lincoln in January 2024.

Missing Israel games 'stressful' for captain Collins

O'Shea proud of how team-mates handled Israel games

Moylan 'comfortable from the first minute' at international level

Moylan joined the Imps from Irish Premier Division side Shelbourne after a stellar final season with the Dublin club in which he finished as the league's joint highest scorer with 15 goals.

At the time of the move, he said it was "the next step" in his career and, after an initial bedding in period and two separate spells on the treatment table with an ankle problem, his and Lincoln's form exploded from November 2025 onwards.

The versatile attacker scored 11 goals and provided six assists last season as Lincoln won promotion and beat Cardiff to the League One title.

His impressive campaign led to a first call-up to the Irish senior squad in May and he marked his debut with a hat-trick in a 5-0 win against Grenada before he was sent off in his second game as they drew with Qatar.

Cardiff came calling in the summer and Moylan made the move to Wales on a four-year deal for an undisclosed fee.

He scored the winner on his debut in the EFL Cup against Swindon and three more followed before the first international break, but he has really kicked on since returning to club duty in early October, proving he has adapted to life in the Championship seamlessly.

Moylan, who has featured as a false nine, a number 10 and off the left this season, has seven goals in his last seven league games, including a first-half hat-trick against West Ham with his first goal a fine finish from outside the box.

His boss at club level told BBC Sport Wales in October that Moylan is a "very exciting player to watch because of how attack-minded he is".

Republic of Ireland fans were treated to snippets of those attacking talents in the first four Nations League games.

After coming off the bench in the defeat against Kosovo, Moylan started the next three games, coming in off the right to link well with Troy Parrott and Adam Idah.

He impressed alongside those two players in the comprehensive win over Israel, setting up Idah's goal before racing through and calmly slotting home.

He was a livewire in the draws that followed against Austria and Israel and is in the frame to continue his burgeoning relationship with star striker Parrott, starting with Saturday's trip to Linz to face Austria.

His international boss Heimir Hallgrimsson knew that he had unearthed a gem from the moment Moylan arrived to train with the senior squad for the first time and hopes there is plenty more to come from him in a green shirt.

"Moylan of course has taken the headlines and taken the spotlight the last couple of weeks and hopefully he can transfer that into the national team," he said.

"His rise has been really fast, but that's brilliant when you find someone in the May [friendly] camp, coming in and scoring three goals in his first game and since then he's been involved in the starting 11 more or less.

"Absolute impact from his first game. Sometimes you need up to 10 games to be comfortable at this level, but he was comfortable from the first minute and from the first training session he had a 'wow' impact."

While it is early days with club and his country, the signs are good that Moylan's trajectory is set to continue on the upward curve it has been trending at over the last two years.

articles.title: Yan Diomande sigue alimentando el debate
articles.standfirst: El jugador brilla por la izquierda con su selección, donde ha explotado también en el Madrid ante la baja de Vinicius, que regresa ya el próximo partido ante el Celta
articles.summary: El jugador brilla por la izquierda con su selección, donde ha explotado también en el Madrid ante la baja de Vinicius, que regresa ya el próximo partido ante el Celta
articles.body: Yan Diomande ha confirmado con Costa de Marfil esta semana lo que se está viendo ya en el Real Madrid desde que Mourinho claudicó y lo puso de titular. Sin Vinicius, el entrenador buscó acomodo al jugador ante la evidencia y se le vio por la derecha, donde ya dio muestras de su capacidad ante el Rayo y contra el Elche en Liga, siendo uno de los destacados. Pero el verdadero salto llegó contra el Villarreal. Mou dejó en el banquillo a Vini, que entraría en la segunda parte y acabaría expulsado, pero el costamarfileño fue un puñal por la izquierda, además de sumar un golazo. Ya no se ha movido de ahí en los siguientes cuatro partidos, con un gol y una asistencia ante el Sevilla y otro tanto contra el Racing. En ese periodo ha jugado también por esa zona ante el Leipzig, con otro tanto y otras asistencia, mientras que en el último duelo contra el AEK Atenas volvió a la derecha con el regreso de Vinicius y dejó su casillero a cero, siendo sustituido en el minuto 67. Con el número 10 a la espalda con su país, Diomande completó todo el partido en el ataque marfileño, partiendo principalmente desde la banda izquierda junto a Elye Wahi y Nicolas Pépé, desde donde robó un balón para asistir en uno de los dos goles ante Gambia. Con Costa de Marfil, el ex del Leipzig es un auténtico líder. Los cuatro partidos de sanción a Vinicius han valido para que Diomande se afiance por la zona del brasileño, que sin embargo va a regresar ya para el próximo partido ante el Celta, en el Bernabéu el sábado 21 de octubre. Es la hora de decidir para Mourinho, que siempre ha visto a Vini por la izquierda y a Diomande por la derecha. Y lo normal es que siga siendoi así si ambos entran en el once. El dilema es que jugar con ellos dos y Mbappé implica sacrificar otra pieza de más atrás, donde Bellingham, Güler o Bernardo Silva han ido creciendo y mucho en los últimos partidos. Mou está convencido de que Diomande puede dar lo mejor por la derecha. Es, de hecho, diestro, y la temporada pasada, en el RB Leipzig jugó bastantes más minutos como extremo derecho (1.591) que por la izquierda (478'). Jugando en su sitio natural, Mou gana más profundidad porque el extremo aprovecha su enorme desborde con su potencia para ganar la línea de fondo y central. Sin embargo, cuando juega por la izquierda tiende más a compagina el desborde con alguna diagonal para encontrar acomodo con su pierna buena y rematar. De hecho, ha marcado con el Madrid desde esa posición, bien en jugada o recibiendo un envío desde la derecha. Mourinho abordó este asunto recientemente aunque no se quiso olvidar del resto de jugadores de ataque pero cree que Vini es el que mejor encaja en la izquierda. "Diomande puede jugar en las dos bandas, Brahim también, Endrick un poco más por la derecha pero también por la izquierda. De todos ellos Vini es el más adaptado a jugar en banda izquierda", confesó. Sin embargo, hay que esperar hasta el duelo para ver si Vini mantiene su estatus en el Madrid. El entrenador confía en él, pero también hace apenas diez días dejó claro que no va decir que va a ser titular. Es evidente que antes de la sanción, el luso ya mostró algunas de sus ideas ante el bajón del brasileño, que sabe ahora que va a tener que pelear para ganarse el puesto. En el club también lo saben.

articles.title: Tebas 'tira' de Jordi Wild y Pedro Sánchez para responder a Uribes sobre la polémica del nazismo y el Madrid
articles.standfirst: El presidente de LaLiga cuestiona la reacción del CSD a sus palabras sobre Real Madrid TV y recupera una entrevista del jefe del Gobierno con Jordi Wild
articles.summary: El presidente de LaLiga cuestiona la reacción del CSD a sus palabras sobre Real Madrid TV y recupera una entrevista del jefe del Gobierno con Jordi Wild
articles.body: Javier Tebas ha vuelto a responder a José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes. El presidente de LaLiga publicó este sábado en X un vídeo que reúne dos intervenciones. Primero aparece el presidente del Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD), que califica de “inaceptable” la comparación de Tebas al hablar de Real Madrid TV. Después, Pedro Sánchez explica en una entrevista con Jordi Wild cómo se puede construir una mentira a partir de hechos ciertos, una técnica que atribuye a la propaganda de Joseph Goebbels. Tebas sostiene que ambos aludieron a las mismas técnicas y cuestiona la reacción del CSD. “Yo creo que es inaceptable, no se puede nunca utilizar el nazismo, Goebbels, como un elemento de comparación con un club de fútbol y menos por el presidente de la liga en relación con un club que pertenece a la liga. Yo creo que eso está fuera de la libertad de expresión”, afirma Uribes en el primer corte. En el segundo, Sánchez se refiere a uno de los métodos que atribuye al ministro de Propaganda de la Alemania nazi. “Y la tercera es la verosimilitud, es decir, coger algunos elementos que son verdad y a partir de ahí construir una gran mentira. Y hay múltiples ejemplos en el debate político al respecto”. La polémica arrancó el 16 de octubre, cuando Tebas vinculó algunos procedimientos de Real Madrid TV con los empleados por Goebbels. El presidente de LaLiga circunscribió sus palabras a la repetición de mensajes, la selección interesada de información y la construcción de un enemigo. También aclaró que su comparación dejaba al margen la ideología nazi y a los aficionados madridistas. El Real Madrid exigió su dimisión inmediata y calificó sus manifestaciones de intolerables y de extraordinaria gravedad. Uribes pidió a Tebas que rectificara y se disculpara con el club blanco. El 22 de octubre, el CSD remitió una petición razonada al Tribunal Administrativo del Deporte (TAD) para que valorase si sus declaraciones podían constituir una infracción de la normativa deportiva. Este sábado, al compartir las dos intervenciones en un mismo vídeo, Javier escribió: “Pedro Sánchez explica las técnicas de propaganda de Goebbels en una entrevista con Jordi Wild, en relación a la oposición. Yo hago referencia a esas mismas técnicas de propaganda respecto a Real Madrid TV y los portaCOCES y Rodríguez Uribes lo califica de 'inaceptable comparación'”. El presidente de LaLiga cerró su publicación con una invitación a comparar los dos cortes. “Misma referencia de TÉCNICAS de propaganda. Dos reacciones muy distintas. Vean ambos vídeos y juzguen ustedes”.

articles.title: Chelsea 1-0 Man City: Sandy Baltimore's winner sees Blues leapfrog 10-player champions at top of the Women's Super League
articles.summary: Report and reaction as Chelsea beat Man City to leapfrog the reigning champions at the top of the Women's Super League table; Sandy Baltimore gave Chelsea a deserved half-time lead; Lauren Hemp missed a sitter in the second half before Ayaka Yamashita's red card for fouling Alyssa Thompson
articles.body:
City were beaten for the first time this season having been clumsy all day - from a lacklustre first half, to wayward finishing in the second to goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita's straight red card for a professional foul. The race for the WSL title is on.

Chelsea deserved the points - they were more at it than City on the day. They had the better of the first half with Ellie Carpenter, Melvine Malard and Alyssa Thompson all going close - before Baltimore smashed the Blues in front with a fierce finish from inside the box before half-time.

City have rescued six points from losing positions so far this season but were off colour in their pursuit of a route back.

Their best chance saw Khadija Shaw hook the ball over Hannah Hampton - but Lauren Hemp missed the ball completely from a yard out with the goal empty, with the effort ultimately bouncing wide of the far post.

And City's job was made harder when Yamashita was dismissed for rushing out, missing the ball and bringing down the electric Thompson - which earned her a straight red card. It could have been worse for City but Aggie Beever-Jones' resulting free-kick cannoned off the bar.

The result sees Chelsea move one point ahead of City at the top of the table, while third-placed London City Lionesses could go four points off the summit if they beat Arsenal on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

4: BIG MISS ! Shaw causes havoc early doors, bursting into the box down the left and finding Aoba Fujino, who fires a huge chance wide of goal.

5: OVER ! Malard does well to hold up a long ball, which falls to Thompson on the edge of the box but she blazes over.

9: WIDE ! Shaw goes on another mazy run, this time down the right - and her cross is deflected just wide of her own goal by Katie McCabe.

10: SAVE ! Malard goes up the other end and her deflected strike is kept out well by Yamashita.

20: BLOCK ! Good work for Thompson sees her square for Carpenter at the back post but her shot is well blocked by Rebecca Knaak, with Malard lurking for a tap-in.

35: BLOW! Malard comes off injured, joining Kadeisha Buchanan as the two Chelsea players to limp off in the first half.

45+4: GOAL! Baltimore gives Chelsea a deserved lead with a stunning strike from just inside the box, before being taken off at half-time.

64: HUGE MISS! Shaw flicks the ball over Hampton but Hemp somehow cannot tap home from a yard out.

70: BIG CHANCE! Carpenter is found at the back post all alone but rushes her finish, which is wildly off target.

72: WIDE! Hemp blazes just over the top corner after being fed down the left wing.

76: RED CARD! City goalkeeper Yamashita rushes out to chase a long ball, but misses her kick and brings down Thompson.

79: OFF THE BAR! Beever-Jones crashes the resulting free-kick off the bar, leaving substitute goalkeeper Eartha Cumings stranded.

90: OVER ! Iman Beney blazes over from a good area after being played through by Beth Mead.

Analysis: Chelsea stifle Shaw as defensive run continues

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at S tamford Bridge:

For the first time in 20 matches, Khadija Shaw failed to register a shot on target in a Women's Super League game, dating back to November 2025.

Manchester City's key striker was pretty much a passenger - bar the chip over Hannah Hampton that led to Lauren Hemp missing from a yard out. But Shaw was the victim of some outstanding Chelsea defending.

At the heart of the Chelsea defensive effort was Lucy Bronze, who was everywhere. She won 12 out of her 14 duels - with that dozen duels twice as many as the next-best player on the pitch. In terms of interceptions, she managed seven. The rest of Chelsea's starters only managed five between them.

Another key player to stifle City was Katie McCabe, who had a brilliant all-round game. Only Lexi Potter (9) made more ball recoveries than the Republic of Ireland international on the day, while her long passing up towards Melvine Malard in the first half put City on the back foot.

Sonia Bompastor highlighted the importance of Bronze and McCabe's role in this win. "Having them, they bring a solid performance in terms of the defensive aspect - but they also bring a lot of leadership in the team to help the others around them as well to perform at their best."

Chelsea have the WSL's best defence by a country mile with only five goals conceded from 10 games. They have 10 clean sheets in their last 13 games across all competitions, having played Manchester United, Arsenal, Manchester City and Lyon in that period.

City may have Shaw but Chelsea have the defensive solidity in this WSL title race.

Analysis: Bompastor wins praise for tactical nous

"I know my player," responded Bompastor when questioned on whether the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan after 12 minutes was enforced or tactical. As it turned out the move was a bit of both.

The defender had taken a knock in training the day before. But it also did not go unnoticed how many times Aoba Fujino got in behind Chelsea's backline early in this contest of fine margins.

Bompastor acted without hesitation. Her tactical management of the game throughout was flawless given both Buchanan and Melvine Malard were lost in the first half. She got the better of Andree Jeglertz, whose second-half changes affected the flow of the game but did little to bring prize striker Bunny Shaw into play in better areas.

Chelsea were pragmatic but Bompastor was equally resolute in her decision making. The Frenchwoman asked her side to be ruthless pre-match and mirrored that bravery in her own approach.

Given the pressure of the opposition and consequences of the result, this will go down as one of Chelsea's most tactically complete displays under her.

Bompastor: An important psychological win

"It's [an] important [win] in terms of the psychological aspects but also right now we are a team who are dropping points against other opponents.

"So I would be more pleased if we were able to win every single game [against the] top teams and [also] the teams we don't expect at the top.

"So yeah, it's really good and it's a nice feeling to be at the top of the table right now, to be able to have won the games against these top sides.

"But I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it's early on in the season, so many things can happen still."

Jeglertz: We deserved more than what we got

"It's small details. It's a tight game, it's two great football teams. There's a lot of situations, there's a lot of battles in the game and they managed to score on their big chance from a great finish.

"We have also a couple of great opportunities where we don't manage to score. So it's small details but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.

"Of course [the red card] is always affecting when you're getting one player down.I think we were on the way to turn it around a little bit.

"So of course it changed but I also think the players dealt with it in a good way. So even though we were one player down I think we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal after we were playing."

articles.title: Jesús de Miguel’s family receive €217,895 after football community rallies behind crowdfunding campaign following striker’s death
articles.summary: After the tragic death of striker Jesús de Miguel during a match, a crowdfunding campaign led by fellow footballer Fran Sol has raised over €217,000 for his family, showcasing the solidarity of the football community during this difficult time.
articles.body: The family of Jesús de Miguel have received an extraordinary show of support following the death of the Spanish striker during a match between CD Tenerife and FC Andorra. A crowdfunding campaign launched by fellow footballer Fran Sol has raised more than €217,000, with donations arriving from players, club executives and supporters. The family have now publicly acknowledged the contributions, while the goalkeeper involved in the fatal collision has been handed a 12-match suspension.Jesús de Miguel’s family thank donors as crowdfunding campaign raises €217,895The family of Jesús de Miguel have confirmed that they have received the donations collected through a crowdfunding campaign launched by footballer Fran Sol, following the striker’s death on November 3.In a statement published by the Spanish players’ association AFE, the family expressed their gratitude to everyone who had contributed, describing the response as a source of comfort during an extremely difficult period.“We have already received the donations from the crowdfunding campaign launched by the footballer Fran Sol, and we would like to express our deepest thanks and gratitude to everyone for this outpouring of love and support that we have received,” the statement read.The family also acknowledged the scale of the response, saying they had been moved by the number of people who had rallied behind the initiative.“We have been deeply moved to see such a large number of people rally around this initiative. Every kind gesture means a great deal to us, and we want you to know that we have received all these kind sentiments with the utmost love”.They added that messages of support had carried particular significance for relatives still trying to come to terms with the loss.“We extend our deepest thanks to everyone who contributed with their kind messages, in words that seemed simple yet carried every meaning of gratitude for a family still living through the impact of the shock, and trying to find some comfort in the solidarity of the thousands around them”.The campaign remains open. As of November 14, it had raised €217,895 towards its €300,000 target, with approximately 5,400 donations recorded. That represents more than 72 per cent of the intended amount, and the total may continue to increase as contributions arrive.Several prominent figures from Spanish football were among the donors. Cádiz president Cristian Siptin contributed €15,000, while Ceuta president Luhay Hamido donated €3,500. Players also supported the campaign, with Pedro Porro giving €3,500 and Marc Bartra contributing €3,000. Alex Remiro and Borja Iglesias each donated €2,500.What happened to Jesús de Miguel during Tenerife vs Andorra?The tragedy occurred on Monday, November 2, during a Segunda División fixture between CD Tenerife and FC Andorra. The match was level at 2-2 when De Miguel attempted to challenge for a high ball and collided with Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, who had come out of his goal to deal with the situation.The collision left the Tenerife striker suffering a cardiac arrest, bringing the match to a halt as medical staff rushed to provide emergency treatment on the pitch. Players and spectators watched as medical personnel attempted to revive him, while the incident left both teams visibly shaken.Owono, the Equatorial Guinea international, received a straight red card for the challenge. De Miguel was given immediate medical assistance before being taken for further treatment, but his death was announced the following day, November 3.The incident prompted an outpouring of grief across Spanish football, with the fundraising campaign becoming one of the ways players and supporters could help his family.Owono subsequently expressed his devastation over what had happened, acknowledging the pain of losing the striker and the suffering of those closest to him.“These are the hardest days of my life. I find it extremely difficult to express my feelings, and I am unable to come to terms with what happened. I feel great pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, of his family and of everyone who loved him,” he said.The goalkeeper also recognised that there would be matters to address following the incident, but said his immediate thoughts remained with De Miguel and his family.“I know there are many matters that must be dealt with, and I will face everything that comes with the utmost respect. But right now, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are living through. Rest in peace, Jesus”.Jesús Owono handed 12-match suspension after fatal collisionThe disciplinary consequences of the incident have now been confirmed, with the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) handing Owono a 12-match suspension on Friday, November 13.The maximum sanction follows the collision during the November 2 fixture, when the 25-year-old goalkeeper rushed out of his area and struck De Miguel while attempting to defend the ball. The suspension represents a significant sporting penalty for Owono, who will be unavailable for FC Andorra for the duration of the ban.The decision comes less than two weeks after the incident, which has left both clubs and the wider Spanish football community mourning De Miguel.For De Miguel's family, the donations have provided tangible support at a time when they continue to live with the loss. The campaign launched by Sol remains open, and the €300,000 target has yet to be reached, despite contributions from thousands of people across the game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
