articles.title: El salto de Pubill
articles.standfirst: El catalán, indiscutible para Simeone, se ha hecho un fijo para De la Fuente
articles.summary: El catalán, indiscutible para Simeone, se ha hecho un fijo para De la Fuente
articles.body: El 4 de junio debutaba Marc Pubill con la Selección. El futbolista del Atlético saltaba al campo en el minuto 59 y se estrenaba como internacional absoluto. Tras una temporada en la que había superado con creces todas las expectativas puestas en él, el de Terrassa irrumpía en la Roja para quedarse. Meses después, se ha convertido en una pieza indispensable para el seleccionador tras proclamarse campeón del mundo el pasado verano. Tras la retirada internacional de Marcos Llorente, Marc se ha convertido en una de las alternativas a Pedro Porro en el lateral y en un central de garantías. De la Fuente tiene donde elegir. Y es que es algo que también le sucede a Simeone con el catalán. Asentado en el centro de la zaga la temporada pasada, su capacidad para jugar y brillar como lateral convierte a Marc en un elemento diferencial. Su polivalencia le ha permitido convertirse en indiscutible tanto para el Cholo como para el seleccionador. De hecho, tras el Mundial acumula 284 minutos de los 450 que ha disputado con la Roja. Tres encuentros completos y unos minutos finales el pasado jueves ante la República Checa lo han situado como la referencia en el lateral derecho en esta Nations League. Con dos tantos en cuatro partidos, Marc ha mostrado también su capacidad ofensiva. Y es que, en lo que va de curso, el ex del Almería suma tres tantos: los dos mencionados con la Selección y otro más con el Atlético. Poderoso en el juego aéreo y con mucho recorrido cuando le toca ejercer de lateral, su presencia ofensiva es constante. Pese a que la vuelta al día a día como rojiblanco pudo costarle un poco tras el Mundial, Pubill es el quinto futbolista de campo más utilizado por Simeone. Con 1.063 minutos, Marc solo acumula menos presencia sobre el terreno de juego que Hancko, Grimaldo, Llorente y Giuliano. Alternando entre el centro de la defensa y el lateral, Pubill se ha convertido también en un comodín para que el Cholo pueda modificar partidos sobre la marcha. Algo a lo que ya se acostumbró Marcos Llorente en su momento y que ahora vive el catalán. De los 16 partidos que ha disputado el Atlético este curso, Pubill ha participado en 14. En 12 partió como titular y solo se quedó sin jugar en dos encuentros: el estreno ante el Málaga, recién aterrizado de las vacaciones, y en Vitoria, por descanso. De esas 12 titularidades completó el encuentro en diez ocasiones, ofreciendo al entrenador argentino diferentes variantes en defensa. En apenas un año, Pubill ha pasado de ser suplente en el Atlético a convertirse en uno de los futbolistas más importantes para el Cholo y Luis de la Fuente. El catalán se ha hecho indiscutible tanto para su técnico en el día a día como para el seleccionador. Su versatilidad es un arma que ninguno quiere perderse. En sus piernas suma ya más de 1.300 minutos esta temporada, en la que ha anotado tres tantos.

articles.title: Michael Carrick breaks silence for first time since Man Utd sacking with emotional message as new era under Pochettino begins
articles.summary: Michael Carrick expresses gratitude to Manchester United supporters following his dismissal as manager, highlighting the unique bond he shares with the club and its fans, and reflects on the recent struggles of the team.
articles.body: Michael Carrick has thanked Manchester United supporters for standing by him during a difficult final spell at Old Trafford, insisting his love for the club “never dies” after his dismissal on Thursday, November 12. The former midfielder's farewell message came just hours before the club confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as his permanent successor, bringing an abrupt end to a managerial tenure that had unravelled after a disastrous start to the 2026-27 season.Michael Carrick thanks Manchester United fans after being sackedCarrick published an emotional statement on Instagram on Friday, November 13, shortly after Pochettino's appointment was announced, reflecting on the privilege of managing the club he had represented for more than a decade as a player.“I've had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love,” Carrick wrote.“There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I'm incredibly grateful.“With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It's different to anywhere else.”The 45-year-old reserved particular appreciation for the supporters, whose backing he said had remained constant despite the team's increasingly poor results. Carrick won only one of his final 10 Premier League matches, but insisted that the response from fans had meant more to him than victories.“I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed,” he wrote.“We've had some great times this year and moments we'll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.“I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.”He acknowledged that the team's recent performances had fallen short, but said the supporters had continued to show him affection when results might have encouraged them to turn against the manager.“I know we've not had the results lately, but you've shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way,” he wrote.“That means more than a win or two.”ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.ID@undefined Caption not available.Carrick also thanked his coaching staff, the club's employees and the players who had worked with him during his time in charge. He concluded by making clear that his connection with United would continue despite his departure from the dugout.“I want nothing but success for Manchester United,” he wrote. “This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I'll always be proud to have played my part and I'll always want the very best for it.“I'll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.”Why Manchester United decided to sack Michael CarrickCarrick's dismissal came after a collapse in form that left United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, and enduring their worst start to a top-flight season in 40 years.The former midfielder had signed a new two-year contract in May, committing himself to the club until 2028 after an encouraging spell as interim manager. He had initially returned to Old Trafford in January following Ruben Amorim's departure and helped guide United to third place in the Premier League last season. That improvement, along with his work in stabilising a previously divided dressing room, earned him the permanent appointment.The new campaign, however, deteriorated rapidly. Across 15 competitive matches in 2026-27, United managed three wins, five draws and seven defeats. They had recorded only one Premier League victory all season, a 5-2 home win over Ipswich Town in late August, and endured an eight-match winless run in the league.The problems began on the opening day, when United lost 2-0 to newly promoted Hull City. A home defeat to Manchester City followed, before Brighton eliminated them in the third round of the EFL Cup. The results left Carrick under early pressure, but October brought a more damaging combination of performances and reported tension inside the dressing room.A 4-1 Champions League defeat away to Como intensified scrutiny of his tactics. United captain Bruno Fernandes reportedly questioned Carrick's approach, while a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth four days later pushed the manager closer to dismissal.According to reports from The Guardian and BBC Sport, the club's hierarchy gave Carrick three matches after the Bournemouth loss to demonstrate that he could reverse the decline. United briefly offered signs of recovery, producing a 3-2 Champions League comeback victory against Roma before scoring twice in stoppage time to salvage a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa.Those results were not enough to secure his position. A 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea, combined with United's continued slide down the table, proved decisive. Carrick was dismissed on November 12, only five months after being appointed permanent manager.Mauricio Pochettino takes over as Manchester United prepare for new eraUnited confirmed Mauricio Pochettino as Carrick's permanent replacement on Friday, November 13, shifting the focus towards an immediate attempt to rescue their Premier League campaign.The 54-year-old Argentine coach steps into Old Trafford from his previous role leading the U.S. Men's National Team, bringing deep Premier League pedigree from memorable spells in charge of Tottenham Hotspur, Chelsea, and Southampton. Known for his high-pressing tactical style and ability to develop young talent, Pochettino arrives with the urgent task of lifting a side that has struggled across domestic and European competition, restoring confidence in the dressing room, and moving the club away from the relegation places. His appointment also brings an end to Carrick's brief spell as permanent manager, although the former midfielder's earlier work as interim coach had initially persuaded the club to give him the job.His farewell message offered no public criticism of the decision or the club's leadership. Instead, Carrick returned to the relationship that had defined much of his time at Old Trafford, thanking supporters for their loyalty and making clear that he would remain invested in the team's fortunes, even from outside the dugout.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mohamed Salah scripts history, becomes Egypt's all-time leading goalscorer with 70 international strikes
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah has added another remarkable milestone to his illustrious career, becoming Egypt's all-time leading international goalscorer after scoring
articles.body: Mohamed Salah has added another remarkable milestone to his illustrious career, becoming Egypt's all-time leading international goalscorer after scoring twice in a commanding 5-0 victory over Malawi in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Saturday. The 34-year-old surpassed former striker Hossam Hassan's national record with a stoppage-time Panenka penalty, taking his international tally to 70 goals in 123 appearances.The landmark came after Salah had drawn level with Hassan by heading home in the 84th minute. With the record within reach, the Egyptian forward showed composure from the penalty spot in added time, chipping the ball down the middle to claim the record outright.Salah leads Egypt's goal fest with record-breaking braceEgypt dominated proceedings at Cairo International Stadium, making a blistering start to the contest with three goals before half-time.Nasser Maher opened the scoring after converting a low cross from Mohamed Hany, registering his first international goal in the process. Omar Marmoush doubled Egypt's advantage in the 10th minute, capitalising on a defensive error from Malawi to put the hosts firmly in control.Hany then joined the goalscoring party with a spectacular long-range strike shortly before the interval, also opening his account for the national team.Malawi had an opportunity to get back into the contest midway through the first half, but goalkeeper Mostafa Shobeir produced an excellent save to deny Richard Mbulu.Salah, who had missed a one-on-one opportunity in the 71st minute, finally found the net in the 84th minute. The forward rose highest to meet an Ibrahim Adel cross and direct a header into the net, bringing him level with Hassan's record.The historic moment arrived deep into stoppage time after Malawi's goalkeeper brought down Hamza Abdelkarim inside the penalty area. Salah stepped up and calmly executed a Panenka, completing his brace and sealing Egypt's emphatic 5-0 victory.Winning start for new Egypt coach Ali MaherThe victory also marked a positive beginning for new Egypt head coach Ali Maher, who was appointed on November 7 following Hassan's departure. Maher began his tenure with an attacking combination featuring Salah, Marmoush and Mahmoud Trezeguet, with the trio helping Egypt deliver a dominant performance on home soil.Egypt will face Malawi again on Tuesday, with Salah entering the return fixture as the country's outright leading international goalscorer.Salah continues impressive form at club levelThe record-breaking performance adds to what has been an impressive campaign for Salah at club level. The Egyptian forward, who currently plays for Turkish club Trabzonspor, has scored nine goals in 11 league appearances this season.His achievements also include a remarkable nine-year spell at Liverpool, where he became the club's leading Premier League goalscorer with 191 goals. He also registered a record 277 goal contributions for a single club in the competition.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: El parón ‘recupera’ el gol
articles.standfirst: Julián y Jonathan David anotaron con Argentina y Canadá
articles.summary: Julián y Jonathan David anotaron con Argentina y Canadá
articles.body: No está siendo el mejor inicio goleador de los delanteros rojiblancos. Tras un verano convulso en cuanto a la configuración del ataque atlético, este parón de selecciones podría servir como trampolín para los atacantes del Cholo. De momento, Julián y Jonathan David vieron puerta con sus selecciones en sus respectivos choques. Dos tantos que pueden servir como impulso para cambiar la aportación ofensiva de los delanteros de Simeone. Julián Alvarez, que se marchó al parón internacional en un momento bajo tras el duelo ante el Barcelona, recuperó la puntería con Argentina. El delantero de Calchín recortó distancias ante Uruguay tras una buena asistencia de Prestianni. El tanto de la Araña no sirvió para levantar el partido en La Bombonera pero si para recuperar la sonrisa tras fallar varias ocasiones claras ante los azulgrana. El gol de Julián al primer toque, similar al que anotó en Stuttgart, viene a confirmar que se desenvuelve mucho mejor en el área de lo que él mismo parece creer. El otro que encontró premio con su selección fue Jonathan David, el canadiense cerró la goleada de los suyos ante Guatemala con un tanto. Antes, había participado en otro de los goles en forma de asistente. El futbolista cedido por la Juventus rompe así su sequía tras un comienzo brillante con el Atlético. Un gol que tiene que servir de impulso para recuperar sensaciones cuando termine el parón y se reincorpore al trabajo con los rojiblancos. El Atlético necesita de los goles de ambos. Y es que entre Julián y Jonathan tan solo suman cinco goles en lo que va de temporada. Dos del argentino y tres del canadiense. Apenas un gol cada 234 minutos. Números muy pobres para los atacantes del Atlético aunque sería todavía más flojos en casa de sumar los tantos de un Sorloth que buscará romper su sequía con Noruega ante Gales esta tarde.

articles.title: Vinicius está de vuelta: se reivindica con dos golazos... pero Brasil sigue perdida
articles.standfirst: El delantero hizo doblete ante Japón en Singapur con un zurdazo a la escuadra y un derechazo al palo largo: con el Real Madrid sigue sin marcar desde el 26 de agosto ante la Real Sociedad
articles.summary: El delantero hizo doblete ante Japón en Singapur con un zurdazo a la escuadra y un derechazo al palo largo: con el Real Madrid sigue sin marcar desde el 26 de agosto ante la Real Sociedad
articles.body: Brasil tenía una nueva parada de su gira asiática y oceánica. Después de los dos triunfos ante Australia y la victoria ante India, los de Ancelotti se veían las caras en Singapur contra Japón. La última vez que se habían enfrentado fue en el pasado Mundial, cuando los brasileños lograron pasar a octavos tras un gol de Gabriel Martinelli en el añadido. Este sábado la historia comenzó siendo bien distinta. Dos errores en defensa condenaron a la pentacampeona del mundo en tan sólo cuatro minutos. El primero sirvió para que Take Kubo se fuera en carrera y abriera el marcador. Reclamaron mano anterior, pero el colegiado no lo vio así y los nipones cantaron sin problema el gol. Sólo cuatro minutos después, nuevo mazazo. Una gran jugada de Nakano por banda derecha acabó en un centro para Nakamura, que pudo controlar con toda la calma del mundo y colarla por el palo corto. Brasil no se lo podía creer. Su juego tampoco ayudaba. Frágil en defensa, nula actividad en el centro del campo y pobre bagaje en ataque. Pero el talento siempre sale a flote cuando más se necesita. Y prueba de ello fue Vinicius. El madridista, muy discutido en las últimas semanas, se reivindicó con un brutal misil desde fuera del área. Un zurdazo descomunal que se coló por toda la escuadra para reducir diferencias. El disparo despertó a los de Ancelotti, que desde entonces se hicieron con el partido. En la segunda parte, Brasil salió con otra cara. Un disparo de Raphinha ya indicaba una declaración de intenciones de un equipo decidido a limpiar la mala imagen de la primera media hora de partido. Brasil resistió, pero Japón acabaría llevándose la victoria en el descuento. Primero, con la izquierda a la escuadra. Después, con la derecha al palo largo. Vinicius sacó a Brasil de un 2-0 ante Japón con dos golazos desde la frontal en el Estadio Nacional de Singapur. Llevaba 46 días sin marcar con su selección, desde el 29 de septiembre. El doblete llegó en pleno debate por sus números con el Real Madrid, donde sólo ha marcado un gol en lo que va de temporada. Brasil apenas encontraba espacios y Vinicius tenía dificultades para desbordar por la izquierda. Hasta que, en el 33, recibió de Bruno Guimaraes en la frontal, controló y soltó un zurdazo que se coló por la escuadra. El 2-2 llegó en el 75. Tras un saque de esquina, Vinicius recibió en diagonal, se abrió hueco y cruzó el disparo con la derecha. Suzuki volvió a quedarse sin respuesta. El madridista había batido al mismo portero desde fuera del área con los dos pies en el primer amistoso de la gira asiática de Brasil, que se cerrará el martes ante Singapur en el mismo estadio. Eso sí, Japón hizo el 2-3 en el un descuento polémico donde Raphinha y Ancelotti protestaron airadamente por las desisiones arbitrales. Les costó la roja. El último gol de Vinicius con el Madrid se remonta al 26 de agosto de 2026, en el 4-1 ante la Real Sociedad. Aquella noche también dio una asistencia. Desde entonces han pasado 80 días y diez partidos suyos con el club blanco sin volver a marcar. Su balance, según Transfermarkt, es de un gol y tres asistencias en 12 partidos y 882 minutos entre Liga y Champions. Toda su producción ofensiva se concentra en el campeonato liguero. En Europa ha jugado cuatro encuentros sin marcar ni asistir. La sanción le dejó fuera de los últimos cuatro partidos de Liga, incluido el Clásico. Su última aparición con el Madrid fue el 4 de noviembre ante el AEK de Atenas, en Champions. Diez días después, con Ancelotti en el banquillo de Brasil, marcó en una tarde el doble de goles que lleva con el club blanco en toda la temporada.

articles.title: Golf over Portugal? Cristiano Ronaldo shares photos with Al-Nassr buddies while Jorge Jesus reveals plans to honour him during Denmark match
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo shares golf photos in Riyadh while Portugal prepares for Nations League match against Denmark, leading to speculation about his relationship with national coach Jorge Jesus and retirement from international football.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo was thousands of miles away from Portugal's preparations for their Nations League meeting with Denmark when he shared pictures of himself playing golf in Riyadh. The timing of the post, which coincided with a press conference featuring head coach Jorge Jesus and captain Bernardo Silva, quickly invited speculation that the former Portugal skipper was sending an indirect message to his national team coach following their reported disagreement and his international retirement.Cristiano Ronaldo shares golf pictures as Portugal prepare for DenmarkRonaldo posted a photograph on Instagram showing himself on a golf course alongside two senior figures from Al-Nassr, his Saudi Arabian club, while Portugal's press conference was taking place on Friday evening ahead of Saturday's match against Denmark.The 41-year-old was joined by Al-Nassr chief executive José Semedo and sporting director Simão Coutinho. The outing offered a glimpse of a new pastime for Ronaldo, who appears to have taken up golf alongside his football commitments.Ronaldo's golf outing came just as Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus and captain Bernardo Silva were addressing the media ahead of Saturday's clash against Denmark, adding to the attention surrounding his Instagram post.The coincidence prompted questions about whether Ronaldo intended the photograph as a pointed response to the coach, although there is no evidence establishing that the timing was deliberate or that the post was directed at Jesus.Ronaldo had spent several days in Portugal, staying at his mansion in the Quinta da Marinha area of Cascais, before returning to Riyadh. His appearance on the golf course came as his former international teammates prepared to take the field without him for the first time since the announcement.Jorge Jesus praises Ronaldo's legacy and responds to Portugal farewell plansWhile Ronaldo was playing golf, Jesus was discussing the Portuguese Football Federation's plans to honour the former captain against Denmark. The coach was asked about the tribute, which is expected to see Portugal's players walk out wearing the iconic No. 7 shirt associated with Ronaldo.Jesus made clear that the arrangements were the responsibility of the federation rather than his own coaching staff.“This matter falls within the responsibility of the Portuguese Federation, specifically my football and sporting affairs departments, along with the president of the federation,” Jesus said.He welcomed the decision, emphasising the significance of Ronaldo's 23 years representing Portugal and the achievements that made him one of the most influential figures in the history of the national team.“I think this idea is wonderful,” he added. “No one can forget the 23 years that Cristiano spent with the national team, and what he gave and what he represented in the world of football, whether with the national team or the other clubs.”Jesus also addressed his own relationship with Ronaldo, explaining that he had worked with the forward for a year rather than merely having a brief professional association with him.“I did not work with Cristiano for a single week, but spent a whole year with him,” Jesus continued. “And therefore I know very well how important he is, not only for the new players, but also for the youth across all parts of the world.”The coach reiterated his support for the tribute, describing Ronaldo as a figure whose contribution to Portuguese football should not be forgotten. However, when asked what might happen next in relation to the former captain, Jesus left the decision with Ronaldo himself.“I think it is a wonderful idea that we continue not to forget that he is a legend of Portuguese football. I no longer know what will happen, he alone knows.”Portugal consider attacking options as Ronaldo's international career endsJesus was also asked how Portugal would approach the attacking positions without Ronaldo, including his assessment of forwards Gustavo Varela and Fábio Silva.The coach distinguished between the two players, explaining that their contrasting characteristics had influenced their selection for the squad. Varela, he said, was a more conventional centre-forward, while Silva offered greater mobility and could operate as a second striker.“The two players possess different characteristics. Gustavo Varela is an out-and-out striker, and he closely resembles Gonçalo Ramos,” Jesus said.“As for Fábio, he possesses a greater ability to move, and he knows how to lead the attack on his own,” he explained. “As I said, he often plays with Borussia Dortmund as a second striker, and for this reason we selected him in the first squad, because we saw that he possesses different characteristics from Cristiano and Gonçalo Ramos.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Mariano de Paco, sobre la nueva concesión del Estadio de Vallecas: “Estamos en conversaciones con la Federación Madrileña de Fútbol”
articles.standfirst: El Consejero habló sobre la situación de la sede franjirroja
articles.summary: El Consejero habló sobre la situación de la sede franjirroja
articles.body: El Consejero de Cultura, Turismo y Deporte de la Comunidad de Madrid habló sobre la concesión del Estadio de Vallecas en la celebración del tercer torneo de fútbol solidario DiscapRayo en el que él mismo participó. “Ha sido un orgullo, un honor para mí poder disputar estos partidos, sobre todo con el equipo de veteranos y en este gran torneo que ha organizado Discaprayo”, comenzó.MAl ser consultado sobre la concesión del Estadio de Vallecas, Mariano respondió que sigue hablando con el club y en negociaciones con la Real Federación de Fútbol de Madrid. “Estamos en conversaciones con la Real Federación Madrileña de Fútbol, que se ha interesado por concesionar el estadio. A mí me parece que sería una solución magnífica”. “A mí me parece que sería una solución magnífica porque el Rayo seguiría jugando en un estadio en el que la Real Federación sería quien se encargase de su control y de su mantenimiento”, continuó De Paco. El Consejero insistió en el objetivo de la Comunidad de Madrid. “Lo que vamos a hacer es arreglar el estadio para que el Rayo siga jugando todo el tiempo que quiera”. Y de que el club siga jugando en su estadio. “Fuera quien fuera el concesionario, el Rayo tiene que seguir jugando en Vallecas. No se puede separar al equipo de su estadio, ni de su afición, ni de su barrio”. Plan del Rayo La Comunidad de Madrid sigue en contacto con el Rayo Vallecano buscando la mejor solución posible. “Nosotros estamos hablando con el club, estamos hablando también con la Real Federación. En cualquier caso, la decisión de la Federación pasaría siempre por la aprobación de su asamblea”, contó Mariano. El cuadro franjirrojo también ha trasladado a la Comunidad de Madrid cuáles son sus preferencias. “El Rayo está interesado en acometer la inversión y en aumentar el periodo de concesión”.

articles.title: La selección española visita a Barrenetxea en el hospital: "¡Estamos contigo, Barrene!"
articles.standfirst: El delantero de la Real Sociedad fue operado de una grave lesión en el muslo derecho que le dejó fuera de la última convocatoria del año con España
articles.summary: El delantero de la Real Sociedad fue operado de una grave lesión en el muslo derecho que le dejó fuera de la última convocatoria del año con España
articles.body: Mikel Oyarzabal, Martín Zubimendi y Mikel Merino hicieron un hueco en la concentración de la selección española para visitar a Ander Barrenetxea. Los tres acudieron este sábado al hospital de Madrid donde el delantero de la Real Sociedad sigue ingresado tras su operación. «¡Estamos contigo, Barrene!», escribió la Selección al compartir el vídeo de la visita. Luis de la Fuente había convocado a Barrenetxea para los dos últimos partidos de la fase de grupos de la Nations League. La lesión que sufrió ante el Rayo Vallecano en la última jornada de Liga le impidió incorporarse a Las Rozas. España ya se ha medido a la República Checa y cerrará la fase de grupos este domingo ante Inglaterra. Según el parte médico de la Real Sociedad, el delantero sufrió una lesión grave en la parte alta de los isquiotibiales del muslo derecho, con afectación del tendón. A la visita de los tres internacionales, con los que Barrenetxea ha compartido vestuario en la Real, se sumaron Aitor Karanka, el segundo entrenador Juanjo González y el médico de la Selección Óscar Celada.

articles.title: Updated College Football Schedule as Ole Miss-Oklahoma, More Games Impacted by FAA Flight Stoppage
articles.summary: The nationwide grounding of all flights by the FAA on Friday has caused several games on the college football schedule this weekend to adjust their start times to account for travel delays.
articles.body:
The nationwide grounding of all flights by the FAA on Friday has caused several games on the college football schedule this weekend to adjust their start times to account for travel delays.

A total of eight games have had their start times impacted thus far, most notably the Mississippi-Oklahoma matchup that had been scheduled for Saturday at 4:15 p.m. ET will now be played on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

Here is the full list of games impacted by the changes and the new start times:

Kansas vs. West Virginia kicks off at 3:30 p.m. ET

Auburn vs. Mississippi State kicks off at 4:15 p.m. ET

Tulane vs. Rice kicks off at 4:30 p.m. ET

Arizona State vs. Central Florida kicks off at 5:30 p.m. ET

Michigan State vs. Washington kicks off at 5:30 p.m. ET

Florida Atlantic vs. Tulsa kicks off at 7:15 p.m. ET

Utah vs. Arizona kicks off at 10:30 p.m. ET

Mississippi vs. Oklahoma kicks off at 1 p.m. ET

The FAA announced a nationwide ground stoppage around 4 p.m. ET on Friday afternoon due to safety concerns from a telecommunications outage. The stoppage was lifted about four hours later, but the travel ramifications remain significant.

More than 15,000 flights in the United States were either delayed or canceled, with the expectation that close to 3,000 flights scheduled on Saturday would alsobe impacted.

College football teams playing road games will typically travel the day before the game. The SEC announced the charter company Ole Miss has an agreement with could not accommodate a late-night departure on Friday, so the team won't leave for Norman until Saturday afternoon.

Utah was also unable to travel on Friday and will leave for Tucson on Saturday morning, but the game will still be played today just three hours later than originally scheduled.

Kansas vs. West Virginia is the only game to move up its start time from 5:30 to 3:30 p.m. ET since the Jayhawks had already arrived in West Virginia by the time the stoppage. The game will fill a time slot opening on ESPN2.

articles.title: La opinión de Álvaro Cervera sobre los 12 partidos de sanción a Owono: "En la ley no está previsto lo que ha pasado"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Tenerife valora el castigo al portero del Andorra en la previa del regreso de los chicharreros a la competición
articles.summary: El entrenador del Tenerife valora el castigo al portero del Andorra en la previa del regreso de los chicharreros a la competición
articles.body: Las heridas siguen abiertas, pero la vida sigue y el CD Tenerife regresa a la competición tras la pérdida de un compañero y los duros momentos vividos en las dos últimas semanas. El equipo chicharrero recibe al Ceuta este domingo y Álvaro Cervera ha comparecido ante los medios en la previa del encuentro. Ayer se conoció el castigo a Owono, portero del Andorra, por la acción que le acabó costando la vida a Jesús de Miguel. "12 partidos es la sanción más alta que el Código Disciplinario permite para los hechos descritos en el acta arbitral", resolvió el Comité de Disciplina. Preguntado por ello, el entrenador del conjunto canario opina que "como en otras cosas de la vida, hay una ley que hay que cumplir y, en esa ley, no está previsto lo que ha pasado. Creo que se han ceñido a la ley y han puesto los partidos de sanción que el reglamento permite poner. Lo demás que yo pueda decir son opiniones mías; me las tengo que reservar y no van a ningún sitio. Puede sonar un poco así si las comparas con otras... pero la ley es así y no podemos decir más". Sobre si la plantilla está preparada para volver a jugar después de todo lo que ha pasado, el míster sostiene que "hay días que estás un poco más decaído y quieres empezar la competición para no estar tanto tiempo pensado en lo mismo, y otras veces no sabemos si estamos preparados para volver a competir y tener la cabeza centrada. Las dos respuestas son factibles, porque no lo sabes".

articles.title: Rakitic: "No soy antibético, lo que soy es muy, muy sevillista"
articles.standfirst: A una semana del Gran Derbi, el croata recordó sus mejores momentos en los duelos de máxima rivalidad
articles.summary: A una semana del Gran Derbi, el croata recordó sus mejores momentos en los duelos de máxima rivalidad
articles.body: Ivan Rakitic ha sido uno de los grandes protagonistas en el XX Encuentro de Peñas Sevillistas. "En cuanto me llamaron hice lo posible para poder estar hoy con ellos aquí. Estoy lleno de orgullo, sobre todo porque todas las victorias en todos los partidos y los títulos pasan, pero el cariño y el amor que siento es para toda la vida. Doy las gracias porque es un día muy especial para mí", confesó el croata, que jugó hasta ocho temporadas en el club hispalense. Momento del Sevilla. "Creo que las últimas semanas son muy positivas. Se ve también una dirección muy clara. Quiero felicitar a todos: al presidente, al director deportivo, al míster y sobre todo a los jugadores porque entienden la idea del míster. Por nuestra parte tenemos que confiar y darles todo el cariño posible. Creo que de derbi siempre hay ganas, así que ojalá sea un gran partido y ojalá poder ganarlo". Recuerdos especiales. "Lo que quiero dejar muy claro es que yo no soy antibético, lo que soy es muy, muy sevillista. Y por suerte hay muchos momentos muy especiales. Uno para mí es el quinto gol que metí en el 5-1, porque a nivel personal es la primera vez que pude meter el balón debajo de la camiseta. A los dos días de casarme, jugué en el Benito Villamarín y marqué dos goles, el Euroderbi… siempre me gusta mucho recordarlo". ¿Volver al Sevilla? "No lo sé porque no lo tengo pensado y tampoco he hablado con nadie. Todo lo que hago se tiene que dar con naturalidad. Ahora mismo me estoy centrando mucho en lo que es la UEFA. Hice ya varios másteres con ellos. Ya sabéis el cariño que tengo al Sevilla y al sevillismo, y a ver lo que da el futuro". ¿Qué espera del próximo derbi? "Un partido muy intenso, como siempre. Creo que el Betis llega en un momento muy bueno, está haciendo las cosas muy bien, así que va a ser complicado, pero vamos a centrarnos en lo nuestro. El equipo viene de semanas muy importantes, creciendo en cada partido. Ojalá podamos dar un golpe sobre la mesa en el derbi". Labor de comentarista. "Intento probar un poquito varias cosas. Fue una experiencia muy bonita con la COPE y también con DAZN. No sé si voy a hacer eso a largo plazo. Me gusta mucho lo que me dicen, que se sienten cómodos escuchándome, así que estoy contento por esa parte" Última visita a La Cartuja. "Muy bonito. Vimos uno de los mejores partidos de la temporada. Comparto la ilusión por el fútbol con muchos amigos que están ahora en el Betis. Me ha gustado mucho ver de nuevo a Marc Bartra y a Isco, que son muy amigos míos. Hemos compartido momentos especiales uno con el Barça y otro con el Sevilla"

articles.title: Pep Guardiola, Thierry Henry or BJ Callaghan? The USMNT’s options to replace Mauricio Pochettino
articles.summary: With Mauricio Pochettino heading to Manchester United, U.S. Soccer faces another defining hire. From ambitious global targets to familiar American faces, GOA...
articles.body:
With Mauricio Pochettino heading to Manchester United, U.S. Soccer faces another defining hire. From ambitious global targets to familiar American faces, GOAL assesses who could lead the USMNT toward the 2030 World Cup.

FAYETTEVILLE, Ga. -- Even with Mauricio Pochettino sitting beside him, U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson began to speak about the future at the USMNT manager position. Pochettino doesn't officially depart for Manchester United until Wednesday, but that doesn't mean the process of replacing him hasn't already started.

That process can be extensive. The USMNT doesn't have competitive fixtures until March, with next month's camp set to go ahead under Steve Cherundolo in a non-FIFA window. Given the four-month break between official games, U.S. Soccer can leave no stone unturned. And, according to Batson, they're already starting to turn over stones.

"Our ambition is high," Batson said," and we believe that this is one of the great coaching jobs in the world. We have an experienced group of players. We've got a dynamic young pool of players...We publicly shared our ambition is to be in a position where we're winning major tournaments, including World Cups, and we want to make sure that we're attracting leaders who help us do just that.

"We know from our experience that great leaders want to work with great people, and great leaders want to make an impact on things that matter. We think that we've proven that, at U.S. Soccer, we are a great place to work, and we're a great place to make legacy-defining impact."

The coaching choice will define legacies, no doubt. Pochettino isn't an easy man to follow, and the road to the 2030 World Cup won't be a forgiving one. So who are the candidates that U.S. Soccer could target to lead the way? GOAL takes a look...

U.S. Soccer has already reportedly made contact , and why wouldn't they? When the best coach of this century is on the market, you should probably give him a call, right?

The good news is that the call isn't without reason. Guardiola has a famous affinity for New York and has been in contact with U.S. Soccer in the past. The timing has never been right, but might it be now? With Guardiola somewhat burnt out and having now conquered three of Europe's top five leagues, maybe? Manchester City's potential sanctions could play a part, too, in keeping Guardiola disillusioned with another European club project.

If the Spain job were on the horizon, this would be a no. If Brazil were there, probably not, too. England? Maybe Guardiola would jump at that, but Thomas Tuchel is still there, at least for now. If Guardiola wants an international job, those would be his three dream opportunities, and none are particularly available.

So, if Guardiola wants to work in something a little less stressful, the USMNT gig could be a good one. Even so, though, he'll have his choice of suitors, which means you can still probably file this under the "unlikely" category.

Big name? Check. Managerial experience? Check. A connection with American soccer? Also a check. In that sense, Henry actually isn't a bad candidate.

The Arsenal legend is also an icon with the New York Red Bulls, and his affinity for MLS, in particular, continued after his playing career as he took charge of CF Montreal from 2019-21. He left the club, at least partly, because he was separated from his family during COVID , who lived in Europe. That wouldn't be much of a hurdle in coaching the international game.

Still, there are obstacles. For one, he has a cushy broadcasting gig that may not be worth giving up. There's also a legitimate question about his credentials as a head coach. Belgian players have hailed his influence during his time as an assistant, but there isn't a whole lot of evidence to point to with Henry excelling as manager. His spells at Monaco and Montreal left plenty to prove, and while he led France to Olympic silver in 2024, he fell short of gold on home soil and has yet to establish himself as a top-level senior coach.

Henry surely has some big ideas, and he has the cultural relevance to get the country to buy in on them. As a result, he should be in the mix.

The other big name international managers

Roberto Martinez? Didier Deschamps? Gareth Southgate? Julian Nagelsmann?

There are no shortage of big name managers available, all of whom bring different styles, experience levels and personalities. Before talking with any of them, though, U.S. Soccer first has to answer a fundamental question: what do we want here?

With Pochettino, the federation took a big swing on a big-name coach with no connection to American soccer. Sometimes, that lack of connection is an asset and, in truth, it could be with this hire. But does the federation want to go down that road again? Culturally and financially, without a World Cup on the back end, does that make as much sense as it did two years ago?

If so, there are no shortage of candidates but, again, it'll depend on their interest level. Some will see the USMNT as an interesting project. Others will see it as four years in the wilderness while the European coaching carousel spins without them close by. It would take the right sort of hire, and only those close to the process will really be able to feel that out.

The in-house option, and surely he will have taken the job knowing that this was a possibility. Pochettino signed a new deal, but many expected that he would leave at some point. Cherundolo, then, would step up in a pinch, take the interim role and, perhaps, win the job outright.

Well, that scenario has become a bit complicated. Due to his role with the U23s, Cherundolo headed to Spain during this international break after being around the team during the first post-World Cup window. As a result, there was no interim opportunity before a four-month break in between international windows. There's camp in December, yes, but that's an MLS-based squad that, ultimately, has little consequence on the bigger picture.

As a result, Cherundolo's path towards the gig looks a bit tougher than it could have been. Even so, he has credentials with LAFC, where he won the MLS Cup. He also has quite a history as a USMNT player and is familiar with U.S. Soccer because of his current role. Those things will have him in the mix.

The hottest American coach right now also happens to have USMNT experience, and it was a good experience, too.

Callaghan has worked wonders with Nashville SC, leading them through a 2026 campaign that might just be the best in MLS history. In Nashville, Callaghan has shown he can be a leading man after leaping Gregg Berhalter's staff to the head coaching job himself.

In between that, though, he also served as the USMNT's interim boss in 2023. He managed seven games before the federation opted to bring back Berhalter, winning the CONCACAF Nations League as part of those seven. He didn't lose any games in regulation during his run and certainly endeared himself to USMNT fans in the process.

That makes Callaghan both a sentimental option and a practical one, especially if he can lead Nashville through a playoff gauntlet over the next few weeks.

An American coach who, by and large, has few ties to U.S. Soccer, which could be a blessing or a curse in this hiring process.

Matarazzo is thriving with Real Sociedad in Spain and helped the club win the Copa del Rey last season. He's previously managed Stuttgart and Hoffenheim and, based on his Copa del Rey success, it would be fair to argue that he's the most successful coach America has sent over to Europe.

Is he ready for this job, though? Matarazzo hasn't been involved with American soccer at any level since playing for Columbia University in the 90s. He knows the landscape, but hasn't been part of it for his entire adult life, which puts him in a weird place between the coaches listed above.

Still, there's no denying his coaching credentials and, if he wants the job, he's worthy of a discussion.

articles.title: Colorado’s Deion Sanders may have just saved his butt by nuking Houston’s CFP chances
articles.summary: Deion Sanders had been on the hot seat as his Colorado football team was in the midst of their second disappointing season in a row. After going just 3-9 las...
articles.body:
Deion Sanders had been on the hot seat as his Colorado football team was in the midst of their second disappointing season in a row. After going just 3-9 last season, the Buffaloes were 3-6 heading into their matchup against No. 14 Houston, which still had hopes of making the 12-team College Football Playoff.

However, Sanders and his Colorado team might have nuked the Cougars' CFP chances after a shock 42-32 win, the biggest of Sanders' stint to date. Per Yahoo Sports, it was the Buffs' highest-ranked win since 2017 , when they beat No. 3 Oklahoma.

The Buffaloes went absolutely berserk on the ground, rushing for 249 yards with five touchdowns. Three of those touchdowns came in a wild second quarter, when they scored on three 30-plus yard runs.

Senior running back Richard Young led the charge with 99 yards on 21 carries with two scores. Young was also instrumental in their big 27-24 overtime win over Kansas State last month. He had 120 yards on 24 carries with two touchdowns in that game.

With his huge win over Houston, Deion Sanders may have bought himself a bit more time in Boulder. This season has been one to forget, with humiliating losses to Texas Tech and Oklahoma State springing to mind.

However, they did give Utah, unbeaten at 9-0 and the current No. 2 team in the nation, its closest game of the season when they squeezed past the Buffs 27-24 in Boulder. That result, coupled with the Houston upset, will give Colorado fans hope that Coach Prime still has enough juice to turn the flagging program around.

articles.title: Jesús Owono suspended 12 matches for collision that resulted in death of Spanish player Jesús de Miguel
articles.summary: de Miguel went into cardiac arrest following the in-game collision and died the next day.
articles.body:
The Spanish soccer federation has suspended Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono for 12 matches after he was issued a red card for the on-field collision with Jesús de Miguel that resulted in the Tenerife striker's death .

"The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report, which states that the player was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play,'" the committee said in a statement . "The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge. "In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances ... the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified."

"The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee's report, which states that the player was sent off for 'violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play,'" the committee said in a statement .

"The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesús de Miguel Alameda, is public knowledge.

"In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances ... the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified."

De Miguel collided with Owono at midfield during the Nov. 2 match and suffered cardiac arrest. Owono was shown a red card and began walking off the pitch. De Miguel initially laid with his head and knees on the grass before turning onto his back. He then became motionless, resulting in an opposing player immediately calling to the sideline for help. Once Owono realized the severity of the situation, he stopped walking off the field and turned back to check on de Miguel.

The match was suspended with the game tied 2-2. De Miguel was transferred to a hospital and was initially deemed " stable despite the severity of his condition ," Tenerife said in a statement after the game. Later in the day, however, the team said de Miguel's condition had "worsened neurologically."

The 30-year-old de Miguel died the next day.

Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Deaths via non-natural causes are open to investigation under Spanish law, according to the Associated Press. Prosecutors have reportedly said it is unlikely that there will be criminal proceedings.

In a statement after de Miguel's death , Owono said he was experiencing the "hardest days of my life" and that he was having a difficult time processing what happened.

"Right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesús and the pain we are all experiencing," Owono said. "Rest in peace, Jesús."

Owono has yet to play since that match. Andorra manager Carles Manso said last week that the team is waiting on the goalkeeper to decide when he is ready to get back on the field.

"He is deeply affected by the situation," Manso said . "We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return."

articles.title: Rafa Louzán, en el V Congreso ProLiga, sobre la sanción a Owono: "Hay que respetar la decisión"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la RFEF habló sobre varios temas durante el evento de este sábado: la final del Mundial, la resolución del meta del Andorra...
articles.summary: El presidente de la RFEF calificó el caso de inédito para el Comité y confirmó que la familia de Jesús de Miguel estará este domingo en el Metropolitano para el España-Inglaterra
articles.body: Rafael Louzán situó en 2028 la decisión sobre dónde se jugará la final del Mundial de 2030 y avanzó que la FIFA visitará por primera vez los estadios de Vigo y Valencia en las próximas semanas. El presidente de la RFEF atendió a los medios este sábado, 14 de noviembre, en el V Congreso ProLiga, celebrado en el salón de actos Luis Aragonés de la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas (Madrid), donde se reunieron más de 160 clubes. Louzán, que no viajó a Praga con la selección absoluta para estar en la reunión con la FIFA, hizo balance de la ronda de inspecciones tras el paso de la delegación por el Santiago Bernabéu y el Metropolitano. "Es verdad que estamos, yo creo, en el ecuador de la visita, porque quedan todavía sedes por visitar". El presidente enumeró las que tiene pendientes la delegación: La Cartuja, Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Vigo y Valencia. A su juicio, la primera parte de la ronda "ha sido excepcional", como ya había comentado a algunos periodistas. El presidente federativo describió el intercambio con los técnicos de la FIFA como "un debate muy sereno". Primero se reunieron durante dos horas y después cenaron juntos. "La verdad es que estoy muy tranquilo y muy seguro de lo que realmente quiere España. Y yo creo que es lo que quiere también la organización", aseguró. Louzán reclamó una reunión entre los tres países anfitriones. "Hay que sentar ahora en una mesa a las tres partes, porque esta candidatura hay que fortalecerla ya de una vez". El presidente de la RFEF quiere dejar atrás la incertidumbre sobre el rumbo del proyecto, ese "dónde estamos, dónde vamos, dónde nos vamos" que, a su juicio, pasará a un segundo plano. Sobre la sede de la final, la decisión que más se pregunta y que, según dijo, ha generado "un clamor" en la calle en España, Louzán indicó que "se va a decir en el año 28". Hasta entonces, defendió el diálogo directo. "Nosotros vamos a trabajar sentados, como a mí me gusta hacerlo, en una mesa", afirmó al referirse a lo hablado con la FIFA. En ese mismo tramo calificó la cuestión de "innegociable para España". Louzán explicó que las inspecciones duran casi un día por sede y que los técnicos revisan tanto el estadio como todo el operativo asociado. Valoró el trabajo presentado en cada visita y aseguró que, en cuanto a operativa y logística, las sedes españolas ya examinadas están "bien encaminadas". Recordó además que esta es ya la segunda o tercera visita de los técnicos. De las 20 sedes preseleccionadas entre los tres países quedan 18 tras la salida de dos españolas, Málaga y A Coruña. Vigo y Valencia se incorporarán a las próximas inspecciones, con fechas por concretar. Será la primera vez que los técnicos de la FIFA visiten los dos estadios. "Ya os diremos cuándo", apuntó Louzán. El presidente quiso precisar el alcance de aquella cifra. "¿Esto quiere decir que vaya a haber 20? No". Recordó que las 20 correspondían a una preselección en la que él todavía no estaba y puso como referencia el Mundial de Estados Unidos, Canadá y México, que se disputó en 16 sedes. "Vamos a ver, finalmente, las que quedan". Louzán valoró el trabajo del equipo de la Federación, encabezado por Eduard Dervishaj, y aseguró que seguirá la hoja de ruta prevista. "Sabemos que es el gran reto que tenemos y tiene que ser el mejor Mundial de la historia, porque además es el Mundial del centenario". El presidente también adelantó que había conocido otros aspectos del torneo que se explicarán más adelante. Felicitó al equipo de la FIFA porque, a su juicio, "tiene una idea muy clara de lo que quiere" y esa visión coincide con lo que España tiene previsto tanto para la organización del campeonato como para el despliegue de la FIFA en España y Marruecos. El presidente de la RFEF, Rafael Louzán, pidió respeto por la decisión del Comité sobre la sanción a Jesús Owono. "El Comité se encuentra por primera vez ante un suceso que nunca antes había sucedido», señaló en declaraciones recogidas por El Partidazo de COPE. "Hay que respetar la decisión", añadió. Louzán también confirmó que la familia de Jesús de Miguel estará este domingo en el Metropolitano, donde España se enfrentará a Inglaterra. "Mañana la familia de Jesús de Miguel estará en el Metropolitano", anunció el presidente de la Federación.

articles.title: Real Madrid superstar returns to form in style with sensational brace for Brazil
articles.summary: Real Madrid have enjoyed an excellent run of results under Jose Mourinho, with several key attacking stars chipping in for Los Blancos.However, one player wh...
articles.body:
Real Madrid have enjoyed an excellent run of results under Jose Mourinho, with several key attacking stars chipping in for Los Blancos .

However, one player whose form has left a lot to be desired is Vinicius Jr., with the Brazilian struggling to get going this season .

In his absence through a four-match suspension, Madrid have continued to improve and have looked like a more balanced side.

However, the Brazilian offered an encouraging reminder of his quality on Saturday, scoring twice in his nation's dramatic 3-2 defeat against Japan.

Vinicius ends goalscoring drought with two stunning strikes

The 26-year-old left winger has endured a frustrating spell in front of goal, with his lack of goals becoming particularly glaring.

His overall performances have also been a cause for concern. However, against Japan, he looked considerably sharper.

With Brazil trailing 2-0, the Madrid winger produced a spectacular long-range effort in the 33rd minute to pull his side back into contention.

He struck again in the 75th minute, curling another excellent shot in off the post to restore parity.

His influence extended well beyond the two goals. Vinicius created two big chances and registered five passes into the final third.

Vinicius also completed four of his five attempted long balls. He delivered two crosses from three attempts, won four fouls and completed 32 carries.

However, the Real Madrid star's display was not enough to save Brazil from defeat, with Japan scoring a stoppage-time winner.

A timely confidence boost for Mourinho's Madrid

Vinicius' timely performance could prove to be an important turning point in his career.

Even though he could not help his team secure victory on the night, he will take a lot of confidence from the performance.

Vinicius has served his four-match suspension at Real Madrid. (Photo by Koji Watanabe/Getty Images)

Having served his four-match suspension following his red card against Villarreal, he will be raring to go for Real Madrid after the break.

It remains to be seen how Jose Mourinho handles Vinicius' minutes in the coming weeks and manages the competition between him and Diomande.

Vinicius' return to form is exactly what the manager would have wanted from this international break, and the onus is now on the player to carry this momentum into the return of club football.

articles.title: Werder Bremen manager Daniel Thioune confirms club desire to sign Niclas Fullkrug permanently from West Ham United
articles.summary: Werder Bremen have officially registered their interest in securing the long-term future of German international Niclas Fullkrug. The veteran striker is curr...
articles.body:
Werder Bremen have officially registered their interest in securing the long-term future of German international Niclas Fullkrug. The veteran striker is currently enjoying a prolific loan spell back in the Bundesliga following a difficult stint in England.

Thioune confirms interest in permanent deal

Bremen head coach Daniel Thioune has made no secret of his desire to keep Fullkrug at the Weserstadion beyond the end of the current campaign. The 33-year-old forward has been in sensational form since returning to the club on loan, revitalising an attack that has struggled for consistency in recent years. Thioune believes that there is a collective will within the club to ensure the partnership continues well into the future.

Fullkrug's impact has been immediate and undeniable. With nine goals in his first nine appearances this season, he currently leads the Bundesliga scoring charts. "The wish is, I think, registered from all sides," the Werder coach stated in an interview with Transfermarkt.de , as reported by Sky Germany . "We as a club, I as a coach and Niclas himself are very interested in working together beyond the summer."

While the intent from Bremen is clear, the situation is complicated by the fact that Fullkrug remains under contract with West Ham United. The striker moved to the London Stadium from Borussia Dortmund in 2024 for a significant fee of €27 million, but the Hammers' current status in the English second tier has changed the dynamic of his future. Any permanent arrangement will require a complex agreement between the three parties involved.

Thioune was quick to acknowledge the hurdles that lie ahead, particularly regarding the finances of a potential transfer. He noted that the English club's willingness to sell and the financial capacity of all involved will dictate the outcome. "What do they want, what are they ready and able to do? And we also have to be honest: What are we capable of, and what is Niclas ready for?" the manager questioned when discussing the logistics.

Despite the financial constraints that often face Bundesliga clubs, the leadership at Bremen remains cautiously optimistic. Sporting director Clemens Fritz and managing director Klaus Filbry have both previously voiced their support for a permanent move. Filbry pointed out that while West Ham holds a strong hand as the parent club, the final decision could be influenced by various sporting factors, including league standings.

"Naturally, there is still a third important party involved with West Ham. The league affiliation also plays a role in the end. But I am nevertheless cautiously positive that it can work out with a signing in the end," Filbry told Bild .

The decision to bring Fullkrug back to Bremen was a calculated risk that has paid off handsomely for the club's board. Thioune reflected on the initial reaction to the transfer, noting that the idea of re-signing the national team striker "did not trigger enthusiasm everywhere" when it was first proposed. However, the forward's incredible goal-scoring rate has quickly turned the tide of public opinion in his favour.

The manager concluded by praising the club's recruitment strategy, specifically highlighting the work done by the sporting director to facilitate the loan move. Thioune remarked that the striker's current performances show "that Clemens Fritz made the absolutely right decision."

articles.title: Pochettino's Man Utd to-do list
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino will arrive at Manchester United next week with an overflowing in-tray of problems to solve as he plots their escape from the Premier Lea...
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino will arrive at Manchester United next week with an overflowing in-tray of problems to solve as he plots their escape from the Premier League relegation zone.

The club announced on Friday that the Argentine, currently in charge of the US men's team, will start work as the new head coach from November 18.

Just four days later he will take his new team, 18th in the league, to the home of bitter rivals Liverpool.

United could be bottom of the table by then, depending on results involving Sunderland and Crystal Palace.

AFP Sport looks at the most pressing problems for the man who replaced the sacked Michael Carrick in the Old Trafford hot seat.

Manchester United must start winning games quickly to quash talk of an unlikely relegation.

Their haul of eight points after 10 games -- with a solitary win -- is their lowest tally at this stage of a league season for 40 years.

The omens are troubling, even if a drop into the second-tier Championship appears unlikely.

There have been 41 teams who have earned exactly eight points at this stage of a Premier League season, and 17 of them (41.5 percent) were relegated.

Only one team in Europe's top five leagues has conceded more goals than United's 30 across all competitions this season -- French side Lens.

United have failed to keep a single clean sheet in the Premier League and have conceded at least twice in each of their past five games in all competitions.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens has been guilty of several costly errors, while individual lapses elsewhere in the defence have also proved damaging.

Injuries, most notably to left-back Luke Shaw, have led to multiple changes in the back line, compounding the problems.

Manchester United chose to focus on a midfield rebuild during the summer transfer window, leaving themselves badly exposed in forward areas.

Their first-choice striker, Benjamin Sesko, has not played since mid-September.

Bryan Mbeumo has been playing out of position to compensate but has just two goals to his name since Sesko's injury.

Marcus Rashford, currently injured, has not managed a goal or an assist since returning from an impressive loan spell at Barcelona while Matheus Cunha and Amad Diallo have been inconsistent.

Pochettino has limited options but he must find a solution quickly.

Pochettino is United's eighth full-time manager since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013 but it is US owners the Glazers and other members of the hierarchy who fans want replaced.

The Manchester United Supporters' Trust issued a statement following Carrick's dismissal this week, pinning the blame for poor results firmly on the ownership.

"The Glazers' debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club," MUST said in a statement. "When INEOS came in (as minority owners in 2024) they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but."

Pochettino cannot change the ownership but he can at least alter the mood music at the club.

To do that he must quickly gain the trust of supporters.

United captain Bruno Fernandes has been the club's talisman and main creative force for many years but there is uncertainty over his future.

The Portugal midfielder, who has been below par this season after a stellar 2025/26 campaign, is understood to have rejected a second contract offer.

United have an option to extend his deal to the end of the 2027/2028 season, meaning he would not be free to talk to other clubs in January.

Getting the best out of United's senior players, Fernandes in particular, will be key.

United fans feel badly let down by the under-performing players after a series of shocking performances.

They made their feelings known after last month's 3-0 drubbing by Bournemouth, pointedly jeering them after Carrick had gone down the tunnel.

The team are low on confidence and with no obvious template despite impressive comebacks against Roma and Aston Villa.

Pochettino must stabilise the team and convince his players that his high-pressing, dynamic tactics are the right ones to get them out of the mire.

articles.title: Liverpool have the chance to finally sign Bundesliga midfielder
articles.summary: Angelo Stiller to Liverpool: Why Stuttgart’s Midfielder Fits Andoni Iraola’s Search for a New No 6Liverpool’s long-running search for a specialist holding mi...
articles.body:
Angelo Stiller to Liverpool: Why Stuttgart's Midfielder Fits Andoni Iraola's Search for a New No 6

Liverpool's long-running search for a specialist holding midfielder may have taken on fresh relevance after the latest update around Angelo Stiller's future. As first reported by Florian Plettenberg, the VfB Stuttgart midfielder is once again open to a move, with a change behind the scenes adding another layer to his situation.

The key detail is significant. Plettenberg reported, "Angelo Stiller and his agency, Sports360, have parted ways by mutual consent. However, the initiative came from the agency, with differing views on the player's future," before adding, "Stiller is once again very open to a move. Saudi Arabia, MLS and Türkiye are also options. Contract with VfB Stuttgart valid until 2028."

That does not amount to Liverpool actively pursuing a deal today, and there is no suggestion of advanced talks from the information available. Yet when a player of Stiller's profile becomes more open to a transfer, clubs who have monitored him previously are bound to reassess the opportunity. Liverpool have been linked before, and the reasons are easy to understand.

Angelo Stiller profile suits Liverpool need

For some time, Liverpool have lacked a pure No 6 in the mould that once gave the side so much balance. Fabinho's departure left a gap that has not been addressed by one natural successor. Different solutions have been used, but none has fully solved the structural issue in the middle of the pitch.

That matters even more under Andoni Iraola. His teams rely on intensity, aggression and a strong collective shape, which places major demands on the player anchoring midfield. The role calls for positioning, ball recovery, awareness in transition and enough composure in possession to launch attacks quickly.

Stiller looks like a footballer built for those responsibilities. At 25, he brings experience as well as tactical maturity, and he has already amassed 328 senior appearances. That volume of games stands out for a player still in what should be the prime years of his career. It points to reliability, understanding and a level of readiness that clubs seeking immediate impact tend to value highly.

Liverpool transfer interest worth monitoring

There is a difference between admiration and action, and for now this remains one to monitor rather than declare imminent. But the conditions are there for renewed attention. Stiller is open to moving, Liverpool continue to need a specialist defensive midfielder, and the fit on paper is strong.

In a market where true holding midfielders are increasingly rare, that combination tends to attract serious scrutiny. If Liverpool decide the time is right, Stiller may yet emerge as one of the more logical solutions available.

This is the type of report that immediately grabs attention because the need is so obvious. Liverpool have spent too long patching that position together, hoping intelligence, energy or versatility would be enough. At the very top level, it usually is not. The side still looks like it needs a proper midfield anchor, someone who makes life easier for everybody else.

Stiller feels intriguing because the profile sounds right. He is at a good age, has played plenty of football and seems to offer that specialist discipline Liverpool have missed for a while. It is easy to see why the Fabinho comparison has appeared, even if expecting a like-for-like replacement is unfair on any new signing.

The price, £41.7 million, also feels realistic in this market. For a player entering his prime, with Bundesliga pedigree and a role Liverpool clearly need to fill, that would not look outrageous if the recruitment team truly believe in him.

The biggest question is whether Liverpool will act decisively. Reports like this can sometimes feel like the early signs of a deal building in the background, or simply another case of a good player being available while several clubs take note. Either way, this is one worth following closely because the logic is there. If Liverpool want more control, more balance and a midfield that finally looks settled, Stiller has the makings of a very sensible move.

articles.title: Why is Mauricio Pochettino coaching the USMNT vs. Haiti today?
articles.summary: The Argentine was confirmed as the next Manchester United manager. Why is he still leading the Stars and Stripes?
articles.body:
MIAMI — Mauricio Pochettino is bound for Manchester United , leaving the United States men's national team job for a return to the Premier League.

But he and his staff are still on the touchline for two more matches.

Games against Haiti on Nov. 14 and Nov. 17 are Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals. The winner of the series moves into March's Nations League Final Four and secures a spot in the 2027 Gold Cup, the continental championship.

With Pochettino announcing his departure on Friday, Nov. 13, the manager said he worked with his future employers to make sure he didn't leave the U.S. in the lurch and without a coach, calling the Haiti quarterfinal "a very natural way to finish our partnership."

USMNT shines in September-October international window

"To be here is an honor for us to defend that badge, defend the players and the staff," Pochettino said at his Nov. 13 news conference. "They understand. I think we need to play tomorrow and the next game. We're not thinking about the result, because we're thinking about performance.

"For sure, they're going to perform and then you know very well that games are games, soccer is soccer and there are aspects sometimes you can't control but we are optimistic."

Steve Cherundolo, a former U.S. international now working as the U-23 coach after leading LAFC, will take over as the interim for a December friendly the U.S. has scheduled with Jamaica.

articles.title: Texas coach Steve Sarkisian praises LSU QB Sam Leavitt: 'He has no regard for his body.'
articles.summary: Two years ago, LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt almost willed Arizona State to upset over Texas in CFP. He's gotten even better under Lane Kiffin at LSU, says Ste...
articles.body:
Two years ago, Texas football coach Steve Sarkisian spent an agonizing four hours or so watching Sam Leavitt almost will a scrappy Arizona State squad to an upset win over the Longhorns in a College Football Playoff quarterfinal. Texas eventually prevailed 39-31 in overtime , but Sarkisian couldn't shake the memory of Leavitt's performance.

Taking crunching hits while throwing the ball downfield? Leavitt did that. Trying to barrel over a linebacker for an extra yard or two? Did that, too.

Now Leavitt plays for LSU after signing in the offseason. That means Sarkisian has to again figure out how to slow down the quarterback in a crucial SEC game Saturday at Tiger Stadium in Baton Rouge, La.

"I mean, this guy's a tremendous competitor, I remember that," Sarkisian said Thursday on a Zoom call with reporters. "He's going to do whatever it takes to try to move the ball forward. He has no regard for his body, and I say that in a kind way. He's going to run the football. He's going to scramble. He's going to take hits. He's going to dive. He's going to extend the ball. He's going to do all the things to try to move the ball forward."

Leavitt has done plenty so far for No. 21 LSU (6-3, 3-3 SEC), which desperately needs a win over No. 6 Texas (7-2, 4-2) to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive. The 6-foot-2, 216-pound junior leads the conference with 283.7 yards passing a game and has picked up another 340 yards on the ground. Leavitt has accounted for 25 total touchdowns.

But Sarkisian noted that Leavitt isn't the same quarterback that threw for 222 yards and ran for another 60 against the Longhorns in that 2024 CFP game at Atlanta's Peach Bowl. He leads all SEC quarterbacks with a completion rate of 70.96%, which testifies to his embrace of a more controlled passing game favored by LSU coach Lane Kiffin.

"I think one thing in Lane's offense is, he's finding those free-access throws," Sarkisian said. "And when he gets those free-access throws on the perimeter or to the tight end, he's going to take those throws. We've got to be mindful in coverage of staying with people. At the same token, we've got to try to corral the guy."

Corralling Leavitt seems a lot easier to say on a Zoom call than executing it on the field. Almost half of Leavitt's passes come off scrambles, said Sarkisian, which adds pressure to any defense. And Leavitt, who also leads the SEC with nine interceptions, doesn't let a bad play affect his next snap.

"When the first play's over, you've got to play the second play because he's going to compete until the whistle's blown, and then he's going to dust himself off and go do it again the next play," Sarkisian said.

articles.title: Francia es la gran rival de España en la pelea por la Final Four
articles.standfirst: El 21 de octubre finalizó el plazo para presengtar las candidaturas
articles.summary: El 21 de octubre finalizó el plazo para presengtar las candidaturas
articles.body: La pelea por albergar la próxima Final Four de la Liga de las Naciones también se juega lejos del césped. Con el plazo de presentación de candidaturas cerrado desde el pasado 21 de octubre, España y Francia aparecen como las dos grandes aspirantes a organizar la fase final prevista para junio. La RFEF ha presentado una doble apuesta de enorme peso, con el Bernabéu y el José Zorrilla de Valladolid como sedes, mientras que la Federación Francesa concurre con las opciones de Lyon y Saint-Étienne. La decisión no llegará hasta después del sorteo de los cuartos de final, fijado para el próximo 20 de noviembre. De esos emparejamientos saldrá la ruta hacia la Final Four y también la pareja de selecciones de la que deberá salir el país anfitrión. La UEFA prefiere que la fase final se dispute en territorio de una de las cuatro semifinalistas, una fórmula que garantiza ambiente, movilización de aficionados y un mayor impacto para el torneo. Sin embargo, el organismo europeo también deja abierta la puerta a una solución alternativa. Si ninguna de las semifinalistas pudiera ejercer como organizadora, la Final Four podría recaer en una sede neutral- España y Francia parten con ventaja en esa carrera porque, además de haber presentado candidatura, son dos de las grandes favoritas para plantarse entre las cuatro mejores selecciones del torneo. Además, la Final Four ya ha pasado por Portugal (2019), Italia (2021), Países Bajos (2023) y Alemania (2025). Inglaterra, potencialmente candidata, es la sede de la Euro de 2028. Para España, además, la designación tendría un valor estratégico especial. Acoger la Final Four supondría un ensayo de primer nivel de cara al Mundial de 2030, del que será coanfitriona junto a Portugal y Marruecos. También serviría para reforzar la candidatura del Santiago Bernabéu como estadio de la gran final del torneo. Una prueba real, con la organización de un evento UEFA de máxima exigencia, para enseñar músculo en un momento clave de la carrera hacia la cita mundialista. El Bernabéu y Valladolid frente a Lyon y Saint-Étienne. Un pulso en los despachos que se resolverá cuando el camino hacia la Final Four quede definitivamente dibujado. El jueves, en Nyon, se sabrá ya cómon son las parejas de baile de los cuartos.
