articles.title: Spain vs England: James Trafford set to replace Jordan Pickford as goalkeeper - but how does Thomas Tuchel stop Lamine Yamal?
articles.summary: Key selection issues analysed ahead of England's Nations League clash with Spain in Madrid; Three Lions will win Group A3 with victory over world champions; Follow Spain vs England in our live blog on the Sky Sports website and App on Sunday, kick-off 7.45pm
articles.body:
The England head coach said before Croatia at Wembley on Thursday that he was quite happy to go full-strength in both matches, despite the three-day gap, and he was true to his word. All the big guns were out for Harry Kane's big night.

Barring unexpected late injury or illness, the best player in the world will lead the line against the world champions. Morgan Rogers should start at right wing, Anthony Gordon left wing. England's Madrid maestro Jude Bellingham will play No 10, and Elliot Anderson and Declan Rice will form the double pivot.

But behind that is where Tuchel and his assistant Anthony Barry will be pondering their options.

Tuchel answered the biggest selection question 24 hours before kick-off, announcing James Trafford will start over Jordan Pickford against Spain in Madrid.

"Trafford will play tomorrow," confirmed Tuchel. "We want to see how far Traff is.

"We give him the opportunity, which is rare. We use the Nations League for that, to see him and trust him in a high-pressure match."

The decision could be one of the most important we have seen for eight years. Since the 2018 World Cup in Russia, Pickford's consistent brilliance means he largely been unchallenged as England's first-choice goalkeeper. Not now.

As he nears his century of international caps (Pickford has 94), Trafford has emerged as the new pretender to his throne. In the last international camp, Tuchel shared the four games equally between the two and he will do the same this time round.

Seeing Pickford walk out at Wembley on Thursday, in the lesser of the two matches, was a surprise. Most onlookers expected him to get the nod against the world champions in Madrid.

But Tuchel has stuck to the plan he outlined at the start of the camp and brought Trafford in. It feels like a real changing-of-the-guard moment for the England No 1 shirt.

In terms of outfielders, no decision is bigger than who should play left-back, to try to combat the most potent of Spain's threats, Lamine Yamal. The man who finished third in the Ballon d'Or rankings stayed in Barcelona for treatment on a troublesome right knee rather than travelling to Prague on Thursday night. He was being saved for England and he is fit and back with the national team now.

Most likely, Lewis Hall will be given the task of keeping Lamine Yamal quiet, keeping his place on the left side of England's defence. Tuchel said after his performance against Croatia that Hall is "doing all he needs to do" to nail down the role as England's first choice and that he is playing "top level".

The Newcastle defender has already proved himself against Barcelona's wondrous winger. In the spring of this year, in the Champions League, he put in a performance that led the Spanish-based newspaper Mundo Deportivo to label Hall the "anti-Lamine".

On the other side of England's defence, it feels like a straight shoot-out between Ben White and Djed Spence, with Trent Alexander-Arnold no doubt expecting to be dropped. Tuchel has consistently questioned his defending and so he is likely to sit out the test in Spain.

Spence missed two England training sessions and Thursday night's game against Croatia as he nursed himself to be ready for this one. He was one of England's most formidable finds of the World Cup, proving himself to be the team's best one-on-one defender.

White has only started one game for his country since before the 2022 World Cup in Qatar and that was the 1-0 home defeat to Japan. If he does get the nod over Spence, both he and Tuchel will hope he avoids the boos which marked his substitute appearance against Croatia on Thursday night.

Alex Baena, who is likely to be Spain's left winger, doesn't pose the same threat as Lamine Yamal on the other flank but he did score against Czech Republic a few days ago - and against England at Wembley.

In the centre of England's defence, again, Tuchel has some big calls. If Ezri Konsa, rested against Croatia, is now fully fit, as he seems to be, he will almost certainly be recalled straight to the heart of the defence. In the absence of the injured Marc Guehi and John Stones he is England's most senior and most influential defender.

Jarell Quansah, who had a howler for Croatia's equalising goal, may well drop out because he is considered a right-sided centre-back, as is Konsa. So that would mean the left-leaning Dan Burn or Jarrad Branthwaite coming in alongside the Arsenal man. Best bet there is Burn.

A significant match for Tuchel's England 2.0

Significantly, Trafford was the preferred choice when Tuchel's men played Spain in September.

For that reason, and also because this is England's final game of 2026, and because it is their last until the Nations League quarter-finals in March - it feels a hugely significant match.

The animosity from large chunks of England's support, and from some England players, towards Tuchel for those now infamous tactical choices of the World Cup semi-final against Argentina, have melted away. The national team's autumn performances have reignited hope and belief.

Which way the result - and the performance - goes against the World Cup winners, will almost certainly dictate the mood and the direction of travel for England from here on in.

In the persistent rain of Madrid, the game will be a barometer of where England are, in project Thomas Tuchel 2.0.

articles.title: Alabama QB Keelon Russell starts against Vanderbilt despite doubtful status due to ankle injury
articles.summary: Austin Mack was in line to start if Russell was unable to go on Saturday.
articles.body:
Keelon Russell ended up playing after all against Vanderbilt.

A day after ESPN reported that the Alabama QB could be rested as a precaution, Russell started in Nashville. The sophomore QB suffered a left ankle injury against LSU, but didn't miss any time in the No. 3 Crimson Tide's 31-13 win.

Russell did spend time in the medical tent during the win, but returned to the field with his ankle heavily taped.

Had Russell not started, backup QB Austin Mack would have made his first start in an Alabama uniform. Russell beat Mack for the starting position in fall camp; Mack transferred to Alabama from Washington when Kalen DeBoer became Alabama's coach and was Ty Simpson's backup in 2025 as Russell was the No. 3 QB as a freshman.

Russell enters Week 11 as a long-shot Heisman contender following his performance against LSU. He was 17-of-24 passing for 206 yards and three touchdowns and has thrown six scores over Alabama's last two games. On the season, Russell is 165-of-245 passing for 2,263 yards. He's scored 23 total touchdowns, as he's thrown 18 and rushed for five.

articles.title: WSL: Chelsea 1-0 Man City - Sonia Bompastor's risks pay off
articles.summary: In any big encounter you will often hear managers say it is the "fine margins" that decide a game. In this case, it was Sonia Bompastor's decisions.
articles.body:
In any big encounter you will often hear managers say it is the "fine margins" that decide a game of football.

Sometimes it is luck. Sometimes it is individual brilliance. But on Saturday it was Sonia Bompastor's bold decisions that helped Chelsea beat Manchester City 1-0.

The top-of-the-table Women's Super League clash was as intriguing as you would hope it to be and both managers needed to be on their toes.

Chelsea boss Bompastor "took responsibility" and brought off struggling defender Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes in, and it had the desired effect.

City striker Khadija Shaw was not able to get in behind like she had done in the early stages, and Buchanan's replacement Veerle Buurman shone.

Was it a tactical substitution or was Buchanan injured?

When the fourth official's board went up showing the number of the player Buurman would replace, there was confusion from Chelsea players.

It was clearly not planned, nor had Buchanan asked to come off. There was no apparent injury as she jogged off and she was clearly upset, heading straight down the tunnel.

Asked to clarify the situation, Bompastor said: "Yesterday in training she got a knock to her head in contact with a team-mate but she was fine.

"She was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine. I had that information before the game.

"But I felt from watching her at the beginning of the game that she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make the substitution.

"I felt I was almost forced to do that. I know my player and she was not in the game."

Whether Buchanan's shaky start was down to that knock is unclear, but Bompastor knew her decision was a risk and was willing to act immediately.

Buurman instantly marshalled Shaw, and City's early threat was quietened as Chelsea regained control and ended the half a goal up thanks to Sandy Baltimore.

Shaw did not record a shot on target and in-form England international Lauren Hemp was quiet as Buurman performed well in a stubborn Chelsea backline.

City manager Andree Jeglertz said he did not think the switch "changed the picture", but he was outsmarted by Bompastor during the 90 minutes.

Bompastor admitted she had not spoken properly with Buchanan at full-time but promised to "explain myself to her".

"I just told her a few words. My assistant coach Camille Abily will have done that already probably and I think everything will be fine," said the Frenchwoman.

"I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I'm always direct and honest so they have the information. It won't be any different."

The risky substitution was compounded by an injury to striker Melvine Malard 23 minutes later, meaning Chelsea's XI was tweaked twice before half-time.

Not normally one to bring on players at the break, Bompastor was smart and hooked goalscorer Baltimore, who was likely still buzzing from her impact.

She was replaced by Maika Hamano, who went on to play the ball through to Alyssa Thompson when she was brought down by City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita, and she was shown a straight red card as a result, ending the visitors' comeback hopes.

"We knew going into the second half we only had one substitution slot and we knew Sandy has been playing lots of minutes," said Bompastor.

"I knew she probably didn't have the legs to go more than maybe 60 minutes and I knew I didn't have more slots after that. I was forced into this one as well.

"It paid off and that's good. Sandy was doing well but she knows the reason why we made that decision.

"That's the first time I experienced that kind of substitution in the first half. It's good for my own experience."

Bompastor's bravery was rewarded and, while City certainly had their chances, Chelsea defended resiliently to see out the narrow win.

Jeglertz could not find a solution to Chelsea's attacking threats, which came largely from wide areas via Ellie Carpenter and Thompson.

Vivianne Miedema returned from injury and looked sharp when she came on for City in the second half, but it was not enough to change the result.

In contrast, Bompastor's risks proved the difference, and they were made with former Chelsea boss Emma Hayes, who mastered the art of bullish decisions, watching on in the stands alongside Sarina Wiegman at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea's victory bumped them back up to the WSL summit, a point above City, while Buurman picked up the player-of-the-match award.

"It paid off today. You have to be brave to make that decision in that moment because you know bringing in a player in the game is a risk," said Bompastor.

"We had a good conversation with Veerle and she was clear on why she wasn't starting the game. That clarity was important for when she came in.

"She had a really good performance against a top player. Sometimes when it doesn't work, it's not so positive, but today it was.

"You have to react and be the one that analyses the situation and make decisions. I'm used to it, even if you don't see lots of substitutions in the first half most of the time in football."

articles.title: Norway 3-1 Wales: Craig Bellamy's side suffer defeat in Oslo with threat of Nations League relegation now looming
articles.summary: Match report from the UEFA Nations League Group A4 match between Norway and Wales at Ullevaal Stadion; Norway won 3-1 thanks to goals from Antonio Nusa, Andreas Schjelderup and Erling Haaland; Wales now bottom of Group A4 as threat of relegation grows
articles.body:
Wales looked the better side in the first half and had chances to take the lead, most notably through Daniel James on three occasions, before they unravelled after half-time.

Antonio Nusa showed why he is often referred to as the Norwegian Neymar as he broke the deadlock with his fine strike into the bottom left corner before substitute Andreas Schjelderup tapped home Erling Haaland's pass to give the hosts a commanding lead.

David Brooks' sublime chipped finish sparked hopes of a comeback but Haaland's penalty, after Connor Roberts pushed Schjelderup down in the box, punctured the late momentum they had gathered.

Wales can no longer finish above Norway due to their inferior head-to-head record, even if they beat leaders Portugal, but can avoid automatic relegation if they are not one of the two worst teams to finish bottom in tier A.

"A reminder Wales have Portugal in their final group game on Tuesday.

"Even a win won't be enough to get off bottom spot due to head-to-head records with Denmark and Norway.

"They will avoid automatic relegation to tier B, though, if they don't finish as one of the two worst bottom-placed sides in tier A.

"A relegation play-off against a side from tier B would be the alternative."

articles.title: Spain v England: Nations League test will reveal if Thomas Tuchel has learned lessons
articles.summary: England's game with world champions Spain will reveal if head coach Thomas Tuchel has learned from summer disappointment, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
articles.body:
England's proof of progress and the lessons learned by head coach Thomas Tuchel since the disappointment of World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina will be put to the sternest test when they face holders Spain in Madrid.

Spain present the toughest assignment England could face, with the world champions' unbeaten run – in which they claimed the sport's biggest prize by beating Argentina in New Jersey in the summer – now stretching to 43 games.

Luis de la Fuente's side last lost - to Colombia - in March 2024, winning 34 games and drawing nine in the intervening period, during which they also became European champions, beating England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.

Little wonder, then, that England captain and Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane describes Sunday night's visit to the Metropolitano Stadium as: "The perfect opportunity to try and prove ourselves."

Tuchel, who revealed Leeds United's James Trafford will get another opportunity in goal as he continues to alternate with Jordan Pickford, clearly feels the same as he added: "This will be proof of concept on the highest level. It's the biggest test in world football. Spain are unbelievable on an incredible run.

"Spain won the last big titles. We are trying to take it away from them. We are up for it. We are in a good moment to push our limits. We are up for something spectacular."

It was a message echoed here in Madrid by England midfielder Declan Rice, who said: "It's a massive game.

"I don't think you can get much bigger than a Champions League final with Arsenal or a World Cup semi-final against Argentina, which I've played in, but when you are playing against the world champions in Spain there is no greater incentive.

"It's the sort of game that brings out the best in us. We want to play against the best teams and the best players. It will show where we are as a group. We're going to see where England are at."

Spain are particularly formidable on home soil, unbeaten in 20 games - winning 15 and drawing five - since a 2-1 defeat by Switzerland in September 2022.

England's most recent win in Spain was a 3-2 triumph in a Nations League encounter in Sevilla in October 2018, their first away victory against them for 31 years.

Yet England came closer than most to piercing Spain's air of invincibility, even though they lost 3-2 at Wembley in September, when a rare Kane blemish from the penalty spot prevented them taking a potentially decisive 3-1 lead.

Spain subsequently punished England and Kane, who will be hoping for better fortunes when the countries meet again in the latest Nations League encounter.

England arrived in Madrid on Saturday evening having reeled off four successive victories since that Wembley loss, the latest of which was a 2-1 win against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

Spain will present an altogether different opposition, but also a barometer of whether England have moved forward since the World Cup, when Tuchel was heavily criticised for what was perceived to be a negative approach in the 2-1 loss to Argentina in Atlanta, especially after Anthony Gordon put England ahead.

Former England defender Matthew Upson, who will be in Madrid for BBC Radio 5 Live, told BBC Sport: "Harry Kane saying this is the perfect opportunity for England to prove themselves is a great way to build this challenge up.

"I wouldn't expect anything less from him considering where he is at now, where his belief level is and what he wants to achieve.

"Harry is achieving incredible personal accolades like the Ballon d'Or, but he won't rest there. He will want a team honour with England, and if you play against the best in the world there is no better barometer of where you're at as a group.

"It's going to be a very interesting test. It's fair to say we didn't see England at full flow against Croatia, so now we will see if they adjust, improve and produce something of their best, which they will have to do if you are going to get any sort of result against Spain in Spain.

"If England get a point, or even better a win, against Spain with their record, at home and away, we will come away thinking they are at a high level.

"If you get a result, you will have had to play really well because you won't do that with anything else.

"By that, I don't mean a blistering game. I just mean doing things well and showing the level you are at."

In the aftermath of that World Cup loss to Argentina, the post-tournament process embarked upon by the Football Asssociation included canvassing the opinions of the whole squad, where it emerged it took place at a "full and frank" meeting with Tuchel at the start of the September international break.

Kane and Jude Bellingham were understood to have given forthright views, where the approach in the devastating loss to Argentina was a key theme.

There is now believed to be a feeling in the squad that Tuchel has taken on the lessons of Atlanta and is focusing on a more positive approach.

Upson said: "England are still a bit of a work in progress. We have two or maybe three players who are playing some of the best football across Europe and the world at the moment. I am thinking of Kane, Bellingham and, at times, Anthony Gordon.

"The key is utilising that, then getting the rest of the team to a place where it can support that and deliver its own world-class support. This is the challenge for Thomas Tuchel."

"England are adopting a more positive approach, but look a little vulnerable defensively, which is maybe the compromise.

"Yes, England could have been 3-1 up against Spain had Harry Kane scored his penalty, but don't forget we could easily have been 3-0 down before we scored."

The intense environment of facing the World Cup holders on their own turf will also be a forensic examination of England's mental progress as well as footballing prowess.

Upson said: "The biggest thing to fix after the World Cup was player reaction and player belief when we're in certain situations, especially if we go ahead and all of a sudden the game is difficult, as it was against Argentina. What is our mindset going to be?

"Since then England have tried to play much more freely, openly and confidently. That's how I see it. That's how we played when we won 7-0 in Croatia. We were free, open, positive. Belief was through the roof.

"This is why this test against Spain is great because you will get tested to the maximum there. If England go ahead, let's see how they do and what they do. If they go behind, let's see what we do.

"Against Spain at Wembley, I saw a reaction at half-time from England, which was fantastic. We should have gone 3-1 up with Harry's penalty, and in that 15 minutes after half-time we were super positive, aggressive in our decision-making.

"This was another ideal situation to test that. They came through that really positively. It would be great if we get another test like that on Sunday.

"It it all plays into what Harry Kane said. This is something which will test people. It's a really significant game for England on a lot of levels."

articles.title: Steelers activate DT Derrick Harmon off injured reserve
articles.summary: A key reinforcement is on the way for the defensive line.
articles.body:
One of Pittsburgh's best run defenders is back to help bolster an already successful defensive line.

The Steelers announced on Saturday afternoon that defensive tackle Derrick Harmon has been activated off injured reserve. Cornerback Terrell Smith was waived to create room on the 53-man roster.

Harmon is still listed as questionable ahead of the Steelers' Week 10 matchup, but his activation is a good sign for his availability.

Harmon suffered a foot injury in the first half of the Steelers' loss at Cleveland on Thursday, Oct. 1. He was placed on IR and missed the next five weeks (four games).

His last full game was against the Bengals on Sept. 27. In four games, Harmon logged 12 tackles, one tackle for loss, one forced fumble, and one sack.

The 2025 first-round pick is a significant component of Pittsburgh's run defense, a unit that gave up an average of over 80 yards more on the ground last year (five games) when Harmon was out of the lineup.

This season, regardless of whether Harmon has played, the Steelers are a top-five unit. Patrick Graham's defense is allowing 83.9 rushing yards per game, third in the NFL. The Steelers only allowed 100 yards once in his absence.

Harmon returns for arguably the biggest game in the AFC this season as the Steelers face the Bengals on Sunday Night Football. The winner will hold sole possession of first place in the AFC North and the Steelers would own a two-game lead in Cincinnati after sweeping the season series against their rival.

articles.title: Jeremiah Smith Makes History, Box Score Stats, Highlights, Heisman Hype from OSU vs. Northwestern
articles.summary: Jeremiah Smith set another record during his sixth 100-yard performance of the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Jeremiah Smith set another record during his sixth 100-yard performance of the 2026 college football season.

The Ohio State Buckeyes star became the Big Ten's all-time leader in receiving yards in his team's 28-19 win over the Northwestern Wildcats.

Smith etched his name in the Big Ten record book again in the first half, when he broke the Big Ten career receiving yards record.

Smith finished off his 11-catch, 117-yard day with a touchdown catch in the fourth quarter from Luke Fahey.

The potential No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft also marveled fans with incredible control on a third-quarter reception.

Smith's 100-yard performance put him within one more 100-yard game of yet another Big Ten receiving record.

Of course, with the impressive statistics came a wave of support for Smith to win the Heisman Trophy.

Smith has two more opportunities to impress Heisman voters in the regular season. The 7-3 Buckeyes visit the Nebraska Cornhuskers next week and then they come back home to host the Michigan Wolverines in one of the sport's biggest rivalry games.
